articleTitle: Mechatronic Design and Fabrication of Aerogenerator composed of Vertical Axis Wind Energy Station with Helical Blades
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: An innovative research, supervised by the Research Group of Advanced Robotics and Mechatronics (GI-ROMA) and the Mechatronics Engineering School at Ricardo Palma University, was conducted, which explored the development of a helical vertical axis wind energy station. The mechanical design of the helical vertical axis focused on determining the blade type to achieve a shear stress of τ=5*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup>, nearly negligible, to let a continuous air flow and obtain a desired voltage output of 5 V. The electrical and electronic design included developing a voltage rectification stage to obtain a regulated output of 5 V; subsequently, 6 V 4.5 Ah batteries were charged and connected in series, with a maximum voltage of 12.67 V, as determined experimentally, which was then connected to a voltage inverter which produced 220 V at 200 W, capable of powering appliances like a 5 W light bulb with a 78.50% efficiency.

publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Discrete Hartley transform (DHT) is appealing chiefly because of its genuine esteemed piece and indistinguishable forward and opposite changes. The components of the DHT grid can be figured utilizing the immediate strategy in which every component of the grid is processed dependent on its definition. They are used to relegate qualities to certain components, and figure as it were a couple of components utilizing the definition. These components are then used to acquire the remaining components dependent on their positions. articleTitle: IoT Enabled Intelligent Parking Solutions for Modern Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: As we know from a few decades there has been a rapid growth of population as a result there is also the growth in the number of vehicles as a result of this people started facing many problems while parking vehicles to find vacant parking spaces which leads to the wastage of time and resources like vehicle fuel. To tackle this problem we have introduced a smart parking system. The main aim of a smart parking system is to use modern monitoring technologies to increase the utilization of parking facilities in large parking areas and also to guide the drivers to an available parking space to make their work easy. It is the initiative proposed to challenge the problems associated with drivers while parking to save their precious time. It is also integrated with an autonomous gate entry system which helps in detecting the vehicle and opening the gate to enter the car into the parking area if any vacant parking slots exist in the respective parking area. This helps in assisting the drivers to solve the several issues associated with parking. The Advantages of the project are Improved Accuracy, Real-time Monitoring Easy Integration, and scalability.

articleTitle: Design & Analysis of a Three-Stage Latched Comparator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: A latched comparator is an electronic component that compares two inputs and maintains its output state even if the inputs vary. This characteristic is especially useful for high-speed analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) as it ensures stable output during rapid signal changes. This paper explores various designs of multi-stage latched comparators, which are designed to enhance signal regeneration and reduce kickback noise, a common challenge in comparator circuits. The three- stage comparator presented shows a significant improvement, with a response time reduced to 306 picoseconds, accelerating signal regeneration. Furthermore, this design effectively minimizes kickback noise, which can disrupt circuit performance. These comparator circuits were carefully crafted at the schematic level using the Cadence Virtuoso tool.

articleTitle: Access Control Mechanisms for Secure Websites
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The research developed an advanced approach toward protecting sensitive information of individuals using a multi-layered access control system in web applications. It integrates traditional authentication and post-login data protection mechanism. It follows a dual-phase security system, first username-password authentication with One-Time Passwords (OTP) for primary login and another PIN system that especially guards some sensitive information inside the account of the user. The architecture is therefore an answer to the crucial need to safeguard different levels of personal data, general account access and highly sensitive information requiring different security thresholds. Our implementation showed that it is able to prevent unnecessary access to sensitive information and maintain smooth user experience on average 8 seconds and 12 seconds in its general features and PIN protection, respectively. It describes how the use of time-based OTPs for the sole purpose of primary authentication along with a separate PIN validation is implemented in accessing the secured personal information. Thus, it is an invaluable input into how hierarchical security measures should be applied within web applications. The results show that protecting sensitive information is significantly improved from systems with uniform security levels to all data types.

articleTitle: Experimental Realization of Single Phase 5-Level Switched Symmetrical Multilevel Inverter using OPAL-RT
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) are increasingly popular consequent their instinct to prompt high-quality output voltages with low total harmonic distortion. Despite their advantages, MLIs often require numerous switches, complex control strategies, and multiple voltage sources, which can expand system outlay and complexness. This research introduces a symmetrical MLI topology that achieves five output voltage levels while using fewer switches than conventional designs, effectively minimizing both cost and control complexity. The adaptation of the presumed MLI is validated through simulations in MATLAB/Simulink) and experimentally verified using the OPAL-RT model OP-4510.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Helmet Detection for In-Vehicle Compliance Monitoring on Low-Cost Edge Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This study presents a highly efficient helmet detection system designed for real-time operation on low-cost edge devices, targeting helmet compliance monitoring in vehicular environments. A novel dataset was created by capturing images from an innovative perspective by positioning the camera above the vehicle’s read-view mirror. This provided a unique top-down view that enhances the performance of real-time helmet detection in dynamic traffic conditions. The dataset comprises three defined classes: (2) no face, (1) face without a helmet, and (0) face with a helmet. This reflected the diverse scenarios encountered in real-world situations. A Deep Learning (DL) model was trained and compiled into TensorFlow Lite (TFLite) format which optimizes the model for low-power edge devices with minimal computational resources. The proposed methodology achieved a high classification accuracy of 99.56%. This work not only concentrates on maximizing the computational efficiency of helmet detection on edge devices but also offers a scalable and cost-effective solution for traffic safety monitoring. By integrating advanced deep learning capabilities with affordable hardware, this study provides a valuable tool for automated helmet detection, contributing to the improvement of road safety rules compliance.

articleTitle: EventSync: Event Scheduler & Coordination Planner
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: EventSync will change the doings in university events organizing. It brings in one-stop smooth workflow, thus bringing in flexibility and efficiency. EventSync presents an intuitive interface of bringing together all three scheduling, task management, and budget tracking in one place. All this reduces tensions and headaches in hand-coordinating and leaves more room for creativity and working together instead of doing work. It further quickens the approval processes; thus, the events can get their way from conceptualization to execution very quickly. Post-Event reporting by EventSync's helps in refining future events with data and feedback from stakeholders. The best optimization of resources, including coordination among team members, ensures that every event is carried out perfectly to create long-lasting impressions among customers. Therefore, when this innovative tool is taken aboard any University, event planning becomes efficient, collaborative, and better.

articleTitle: Automatic Emotion Detection from Facial Features Extraction and Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In the domain of Interactive Systems (IS), machine learning (ML) emerges as a profound, user-friendly, and accurate approach to enhancing emotional intelligence in digital systems. This research work focuses on facial emotion detection, an important but often-neglected aspect of affective computing. Models used for the assessment include Multinomial Naïve Bayes (MNB), Decision Trees (DT), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), XG Boost (XGB), and Logistic Regression (LR). By employing the FER2013 dataset and MediaPipe’s (MP’s) facial recognition technology, this research extracts 478 3D facial landmarks to test. The best Acc in emotion detection is found using LR with an accuracy of 65.57% followed by XGB with an accuracy of 61.24%. This study thus will help as a practical application toward making improvements in IS in matters regarding health, marketing, or even security.

articleTitle: Graph Representation Learning for Recommender Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Graph data represents information efficiently and can be used to learn subsequent tasks easily. In the domain of biological science, recommender systems, social network analysis graph representation learning has become ubiquitous with tremendous success. A graph structured data can make a system to learn, produce new information and can be analyzed for set of tasks. Deep learning-based recommender systems are using deep graph embeddings for improved accuracy by exploring user item relations. This relation exploration can be utilized for other recommendation task such as link prediction. In this study we are providing overview of graph representation learning with complete analysis of data with graph representation. This study provides importance of graph representation in recommender system to learn node representations. The results and discussion section denotes how simple graph neural network technique successfully applied on graph data for node representation learning and challenges.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Hybrid Wired/Wireless charging system for Electric Vehicle applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The rapid deployment of wired charging stations has enabled the quick adaption of electric vehicles by consumers. The simplicity in modelling and control of wired charger makes it well established in EV industry. It also produces efficiency in the desired range. However, convenience is the key issue. On the other hand, wireless charging has benefits like safe isolation between the coils and the possibility of charging the vehicle when in motion. Therefore, in this article, a combination of wired and wireless charging method is put forth in order to make the charging infrastructure compatible to all charging setups efficiently. Further, the proposed system operates in four modes, where two modes allow power flow from Grid-to-vehicle and the other two modes allow vehicle-to-grid power flow. A 3.7kW hybrid charger is designed and experimented and the performance of the proposed hybrid charger is presented.

articleTitle: OMR Sheet Analysing Using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: For years, Optical Mark Recognition (OMR) have utilized to extract data through paper-based forms. However, analyzing OMR sheets by hand is time-consuming and prone to human error. This study introduces a sophisticated method which combines advance image processing and neural learning techniques to systematize OMR sheet breakdown. The proposed design exactly identifies and marks responses on the bubbled sheets through the application of image enhancement, segmentation, and feature extraction algorithms. To assess individual and group performance, a performance analysis is conducted, offering valuable insights for educators and researchers. Various imaging methods, including Median filtering, RGB to Grey conversion, edge detection, and complement of image, are employed to evaluate the sheet and display the final score based on the selected responses for each question. This approach eliminates the need for bulky equipment and expensive scanners, resulting in time and cost savings. Advanced algorithms and preprocessing techniques are used to address complex issues related to noisy image, marking variations, alignment of sheets Through extensive experimentation besides comparison, the system validates its greater accuracy and effectiveness likened to method of manual analysis. The paper also explores potential future improvements, such as cloud-based combination and instantaneous analysis, prominence the system's capacity aimed at greater automation and reliability in valuation process.

articleTitle: Evaluating Optimization Strategies for Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems in Power Generation: A Critical Review
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In the current scenario, the increasing energy demand due to the growing population poses a significant challenge as limited fossil fuel reserves are hardly able to meet this growing demand sustainably. Renewable energy technologies offer a promising path forward, especially in off-grid regions where expanding the grid is both costly and complex. Hybrid renewable energy systems, which integrate multiple renewable sources, provide enhanced reliability, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness compared to single-source systems. These systems are gaining traction globally, with the market growing rapidly. This paper examines a range of optimization strategies that aim to improve the efficiency of hybrid renewable energy systems in power generation.

articleTitle: Sustainability Effectiveness using Lean Manufacturing Tools for Production Engineering on Metal-mechanic Industry: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This systematic review analyzes the impact of Lean Manufacturing tools on the productivity of companies in the metal-mechanical sector. The PRISMA method was used, which was carried out, resulting in 14 articles. The database used for the review was Scopus and the results showed that Lean has a positive impact on productivity, since there were indicators that showed significant changes such as: a reduction in production time, increase in operational efficiency, reduction of defective parts, and inventory reduction. However, its success depends on factors such as training and adaptation to specific contexts. Some limitations that were found in the review were: the majority of articles were from the continent of Asia and Europe, and all the articles were from research published in the English language. Finally, some suggestions are provided for future reviews that develop the same topic.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of 6T SRAM : A Comparative Study of Conventional and Stacking Techniques in 45nm Technology using cadence virtuoso
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth examination of 6T SRAM (Static Random Access Memory) architectures within the 45nm technology node, with a particular emphasis on optimizing power consumption and delay characteristics. Both traditional 6T SRAM and stacked 6T SRAM structures are evaluated through comprehensive simulations performed in Cadence Virtuoso, enabling a detailed comparison of average power and delay across varied operational parameters, like supply voltage (VDD). The results indicate that the stacked 6T SRAM configuration achieves notable gains in power efficiency and operational speed, especially at reduced VDD levels, underscoring its suitability for future low- power applications. This study not only advances the understanding of key trade-offs in SRAM design but also offers a valuable framework for further refinement of SRAM technologies. [1]

articleTitle: Enhanced Multi-Reference Real-Time Object Detection using Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid development of Electric Vehicles has been used worldwide to sustain the environment and to reduce dependency on fuel. These cars have batteries which can last up to 10-20 years. With the enormous growth of Electric Vehicles, many charging stations have been established. However, the charging cable weighing 1-2kg is a challenge for the user to handle each time. Therefore, the need for automated charging stations is the focal area of research. In this paper, we developed a system using OpenCV to detect the type of charging port and compare it to a reference database which enables the Automatic Charging System to use the specific charger without manual labor.

articleTitle: Track Sensing Obstacle Avoidance Technology For Autonomous Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents a developed and tested autonomous robotic vehicle with a track sensing and obstacle avoidance system, using an L298 motor driver and an Arduino Nano. The vehicle is designed to move autonomously in different environments while detecting obstacles and making avoidance decisions. It is fitted with an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor, which continuously measures the distance for the presence of an obstacle and changes the path of the vehicle accordingly. The motor driver L298 controls the two DC motors, which aid in controlling the movement of the robot accurately. The Arduino Nano microcontroller then processes this information from the ultrasonic sensor and instructs the motor driver to make adjustments to achieve a smooth navigation and obstacle avoidance in real-time. Designed for handling various types of terrains and obstacles, the robot showcases very advanced techniques of collision avoidance. The control software is written in the Arduino IDE and C++ programming, integrating sensor information with motor commands. This project is for improving efficiency and autonomy in terms of robotic vehicles, with absolutely no manual intervention to the least possible while improving operational reliability.

articleTitle: Different MPPT Algorithms for DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The efficient and appropriate power flow technologies are necessary for better performance of renewable energy system applications. The comparative study of different MPPT algorithms, which are best for RES applications due to their influence on efficiency, low response time and the stability under different intervals of irradiance and temperature. When comes to this context, the key focus is evaluation of algorithms to the converter which is bidirectional by considering the desired operational conditions. The observations of this study are a forward step to optimization of systems with bidirectional converters in improving the reliability and sustainability.

articleTitle: Development of robotic arm for fruits and vegetables sorting
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Among various automation approaches, the pick and-place robotic arm stands out due to its versatility and potential for wide application in sorting, picking, and placing tasks. The robotic arm is equipped with advanced computer vision capabilities for automated agricultural tasks. The system incorporates object detection algorithms using THONY software to accurately identify and localize fruits or vegetables within the arm's workspace. The integration of object detection and classification enhances the system's versatility and adaptability, making it suitable for agricultural applications which includes sorting. By automating repetitive tasks and utilizing real-time object detection, the robotic arm enhances operational efficiency, reduces labor requirements, and improves precision in handling and sorting.

articleTitle: Hybrid Ensemble of MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 for Enhanced Land Use and Land Cover Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In this research, we instigated a composite neural network approach by integrating MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 models to boost the precision and efficiency of land use and land cover (LULC) classification. Utilizing the NWPU-RESISC45 dataset and SIRI-WHU, which encompasses a diverse set of remote-sensing images across 12 distinct classes, our model leverages MobileNetV2’s efficient architecture and EfficientNet-B0’s high accuracy. The combined model achieved a notable 98.3% and 96.04% accuracy respectively for the datasets, affirming its effectiveness and robustness in categorizing various types of land cover in complex scenes. This performance highlights the model’s potential for scalable, real-time environmental monitoring and urban planning.

articleTitle: Tracking Dynamic Facial Function in Facial Palsy Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This research introduces a machine learning-based approach for assessing dynamic facial function in facial palsy patients through objective iris movement tracking. Integrated with a remote monitoring application, this method aims to improve diagnostic accuracy and optimize outcomes in enhancing patient quality of life. The proposed system leverages real-time video analysis to capture subtle iris and facial muscle movements, which are essential indicators of facial nerve health. By offering remote accessibility, it facilitates early detection and personalized treatment recommendations, bridging gaps in care for patients with limited access to specialized facilities. This approach has the potential to advance clinical practices by providing a standardized, non-invasive, and efficient tool for monitoring and evaluating facial palsy recovery.

articleTitle: Induction Motor Controller and Protection System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Induction motors are extensively used in artificial and marketable operations due to their robustness and effectiveness. To maximize performance and achieve long life from them, speed control and protection systems are necessary. In this paper, the study is to examine an induction motor regulator as a DOL starter, star-delta starter, VFD, and soft starters, which were compactly studied with a complete review about their appearance, features, and control about speed as well as direction, and also cover some protection results similar as load, short-circuit, phase failure, overvoltage, and undervoltage protections. In order to help damage by electrical and mechanical irregularities, these systems work together to increase operability, trust ability, and safety.

articleTitle: IoT Based Portable Multi-Purpose Biometric Authentication System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This research paper aims to contribute to the field of biometric attendance systems. Biometric system which uses unique biological traits like fingerprints for identification and authentication, offers several benefits over traditional authentication methods like passwords or ID cards. The benefits of using biometric system can be enhanced security, convenience and high efficiency, reduced risk of fraud, cost-effective in long run, accountability, scalability, multi-factor authentication, etc. In most of the organizations or institutes attendance is taken by the traditional methods like register book but this method takes time then attendance from these registers is uploaded to server for further attendance report of students. To withstand this problem, we have proposed an IoT based multipurpose biometric authentication system. We have developed a portable system that includes fingerprint sensors to recognize the fingerprint of various students and show the details of the students whose fingerprints have been scanned. The data from the fingerprint scanner is sent to the Raspberry PI server using Wi-Fi. We also have also designed a user interface for students and faculty to view and manage the students and their attendance. The attendance report can be exported to excel file any time faculty want the report. The biometric system provides 80% efficiency over the regular attendance methods.

articleTitle: Optimized Image Processing on FPGAs: Comparative Analysis of Adder Architectures for Image Smoothing Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Image smoothening is a highly utilized operation in digital image processing focused on reducing the impact of noise. In field programmable gate arrays (FPGA) based implementation, the working of the image smoothening process depends on the arithmetic components, particularly the adder structures. Modifying the underlying adder structures would have a significant impact on the efficiency of image processing. This paper presents a comparative analysis of four advanced adder architectures - like optimized lower part constant or adder (OLOCA), hardware optimized approximate adder with normal error distribution (HOAANED), brent-kung adder, and kogge-stone adder - against the conventional ripple carry adder (RCA). Different adder’s impact is evaluated based on delay, power consumption, resource utilization, and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). Our findings demonstrate how selecting an optimal adder can impact the performance of FPGA-based image-smoothening applications.

articleTitle: Critical Contingency Assessment of a 150/275 kV Interconnected Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The 150/275 kV Southern Sumatra Interconnected System (in Bahasa: Sumbagsel) is crucial for providing reliable and sustainable electricity to the region. As network complexity and energy demand grow, challenges related to dynamic security intensify. This study assesses the system's ability to maintain stability during disturbances. Analyses using DIgSILENT PowerFactory software evaluated system responses to fault scenarios, particularly large generator losses, focusing on rotor angle, system frequency, and bus voltage after disturbances. Results show that the Sumbagsel interconnection has critical points prone to dynamic instability. While the system can remain stable within safe limits if disturbances don't exceed handling capacity, mitigation measures like improved coordination between generation and transmission networks are necessary. This study aims to enhance the power system's reliability in the region and prepare it for future operational challenges.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning Ensembles for Stock Index Forecasting: A Nifty 50 approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: A plethora of research is carried out in the field of investment decision-making but is still a non-conquered territory owing to the data complexity and uncertainty involved in the financial market. In this research, two ensemble models are developed and assessed unifying two deep learning models as base learners to form Ensemble 1: CNN+LSTM and Ensemble 2: TCN+LSTM. A stacked ensemble approach is considered using Linear regressor as meta learner with input from the base learners’ output for final prediction. The study utilizes Nifty 50 index historical data, for the empirical study. Based on benchmark comparison with single models CNN, TCN, and LSTM, the ensemble models performed better, with Ensemble 2 giving better outputs than Ensemble 1. Model evaluation is done using five performance metrics. Furthermore, models are validated through 5-fold cross-validation adding robustness to the findings and analysis.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Classification Techniques for News Data
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In the digital world, there is a large amount of online news sources which creates a problem to users to navigate and get the updated information from the News content management. This is a machine learning project which is creating a way to allow articles to be intelligently categorized, so it’s simpler to locate those news pieces that are important to you. Additionally, the scalability of each approach will be investigated to determine the suitability for processing large scale news datasets. The purpose of our approach is to classify news article to a relevant topic such that the news articles are grouped and users have a better experience in news platform. Using these performance metrics, this technology has real potential to streamline news management and increase user engagement to the next level. Furthermore, the project also investigates the idea of leveraging natural language processing (NLP) methods to further augment classification accuracy and to better extract the true semantic meaning of the news articles. We preprocessing the data by using natural language processing (NLP) techniques such as cleaning, tokenization, lemmatization and word embedding using TF- IDF vectorizer. Then we split the data and train an ANN and Gaussian Naive Bayes. Overall, this work was meant to make towards the development of a safe and effective device for automated grouping of on the web news articles so that it will certainly be simpler for individuals to access appropriate information in the dense environment of online media.

articleTitle: Analysis of Capacity Utilization Factor of Decentralized Solar Generators: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This study analyzes the Capacity Utilization Factor (CUF) of solar power plants under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) scheme in four districts of Madhya Pradesh, India: Tikamgarh, Panna, Sagar, and Damoh. The analysis reveals significant CUF variations across districts, with some plants exhibiting consistently low performance. Factors influencing CUF include solar irradiance, equipment efficiency, grid connectivity, and maintenance practices. Seasonal variations, particularly during winter months with reduced solar radiation, significantly impacted CUF in all regions. Key recommendations to improve CUF include enhancing post-installation support, optimizing plant design and maintenance, promoting grid connectivity and reliability, and leveraging technology for real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance. This study emphasizes the critical role of CUF analysis in assessing the performance of KUSUM solar plants. It provides valuable insights for optimizing the scheme's effectiveness and ensuring the long-term viability of these projects for farmers.

articleTitle: Minimize THD of Variable Load Conversion based Wind Energy System using Three-phase Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Nature has an abundance of renewable energy source including wind. Electricity systems powered by Worldwide interest in wind energy is growing due to the economic and environmental advantages they offer. To utilize wind energy a WECS is necessary, which is comprised a power electric converter, an electric generator, wind turbine blades, and the associated control system. Different WECS configurations can be achieved through the use of stall-regulated or pitch-regulated systems and synchronous or asynchronous machines. These systems' functional objective is to transform wind energy into electrical power and feed it into a utility grid. The entire set of frameworks will include: The greatest power point after control, a wind turbine model with gearbox and pitch control, model of a multiphase machine, Three-level T-type inverters arranged consecutively, PLL for network-side inverter synchronization, voltage-positioned control for lattice-side inverter control, and aberrant rotor field-situated control for machine-side converter control.

articleTitle: Automated Pesticide Sprayer Using Smart Agribot
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: A wireless sensor network has been developed to help farmers spray pesticides on their crops, reducing air pollution caused by insecticide use. The bot, which uses mobile phones to control the spray, sprays the pesticides on all plants on the farm, reducing time and work for farmers. The bot uses machine learning to analyze input images and predict remedies for diseases on leaves, stems, or plants. The L293d motor driver moves the robot, while the Raspberry Pi 3 processor is used for the embedded system. Python code is used for machine learning, training the robot with pre-defined images. This remote control system allows farmers to stay unaffected by their health condition and work more efficiently, reducing their time and effort in agriculture. The main goal of this paper to improve the efficiency of pesticide use by the bot and reduce the environmental impact on farmers.

articleTitle: One Step Toward Touch Automation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Functional validation is the process in which the SoC design is tested after the manufacture of the chip. In industry, many engineers work on the functional validation and test the different IPs using different techniques. There are several responsibilities which come under the account of a functional validation engineer. Taking care of the resources and equipment which will be useful at the time of validation is one of the responsibilities. Touch Host Controller (THC) is one of the IPs, where the engineer has to test the touch panel and touch handling capability of the SoC. Such testing requires the touch panel. The Functional Validation Engineer has to order these materials well in advance in order to ensure timely execution of the validation.There are however situations where the required display panel may not be available in time, and as every project has deadlines, as engineers may not be able for the touch panel. What can be the solution in such cases?In this paper, a solution is proposed to handle a situation where a touch panel is not readily available for testing. The solution will try to replace the touch panel with a microcontroller that emulates the touch interface of a touch panel. This allows the touch panel to be replaced and testing to proceed in its absence. The solution proposes the Microchip’s ARM Cortex M0+ AT SAMD21J18A controller to emulate the touch panel to send the data using the HID over I2C protocol.

articleTitle: Automated Waste Segregation: Transforming Scrap Processing in the Recycling Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Waste management that works well is a big problem worldwide made worse by cities growing fast and more factories popping up. This paper looks at systems that sort waste focusing on ones that use Arduino for the scrap business. Sorting waste matters a lot to recycle well and keep the environment healthy, and old ways often don't cut it in factories. The new system we're talking about uses special sensors and an Arduino brain to tell apart and separate metal, glass, and plastic trash. This paper checks out what tech and methods are out there now, shows how we set up our test, and looks at how well it works - like how good it is at spotting different materials and how it runs. By bringing in machines to sort waste, this system doesn't just work better - it also helps recycle more stuff. What we found shows that these automatic systems could help with waste problems and points to where we might go next with this tech.

articleTitle: Haptic Social Connectivity and Navigation: Smart Glasses for Enhancing Interaction Among the Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The purpose of the project is to create smart glasses for people who are visually impaired to help them improve social interaction and help them in navigation as well. Haptic feedback devices are incorporated in the eyeglasses which assist in communication using facial expressions through the Deepface library embedded. This allows them to understand the emotions of people shown in the video feed from the camera as replications of seven emotions: sadness, fear, disgust, happiness, surprise, neutrality, and anger. Each of these emotions is represented by a different rhythm of vibration allowing the glasses to communicate something different for each emotion. In addition to this, ultrasonic sensors pick up other people or objects that are in close range, indicating the direction from which they are approaching. As the objects move closer, there is a corresponding increase in the vibration intensity, with almost the strongest level being felt when the object is within close range ensuring safety and upper body awareness. To avoid confusion between the two types of haptics, a special button is used so that the users can easily switch between the two modes. The device consists of a Raspberry Pi 4, motors for vibration, a camera connected with a USB, and computer vision technologies such as OpenCV.

articleTitle: An Attention-Driven Bi-GRU Framework for India VIX Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The India VIX, as a measure of market volatility, has significant implications for decision-making processes and necessary risk control measures, among other things; hence, it is essential to predict it accurately. In this paper, an attention-enhanced BI-GRU model for predicting the closing price of India VIX is introduced. Through the application of an additive attention mechanism, dependencies over time are incorporated and crucial features are emphasized in the input. The analysis of the findings demonstrated that the suggested attention-enhanced BI-GRU model outperformed the baseline models for prediction accuracy and dependability. The relevance and usefulness of the model were further affirmed by the visualizations such as the prediction and the loss function graphs. The real-world importance of this research is to the potential application of its findings in risk analysis and the tactical and strategic control of financial flows.

articleTitle: An FFT Accelerator IP Core Implemented on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The main objective of this project is to design and implement a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) IP core. Due to its ability to provide accurate frequency domain analysis of time domain signals, the FFT technique is indispensable in many applications related to digital signal processing. The implementation is based on the radix-2 method, whose lower computational complexity and hardware resource efficiency make it a good fit for FPGA platforms. With its robust FPGA and ARM CortexA53 processors, the ZCU104 board provides an adaptable environment for creating unique IP cores and incorporating them into more complex systems.The objective of this project is to use the Zynq SoC’s hardware acceleration capabilities to improve the FFT core for speed and resource consumption. The ZCU104 board is used to test and validate the built IP core, proving its usefulness for real-time signal processing applications. As compared to software-based FFT implementations, the results demonstrate a notable boost in performance, underscoring the potential of FPGA based solutions in high performance computing jobs.

articleTitle: Preserving Diagnostic Quality of Image Compression using Block Adaptive Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Information compression is shown to pack the size of data accumulated in advanced documents. We have proposed a block adaptive model (BAM) compression strategy to pack the size of image while keeping the decompression overhead insignificant. In versatile lossless word reference based image compression, when compression proportion is looked at among word reference based methodology. To inspect the presentation of the Lossless and Lossy compression of images and to get high pressure proportion for both lossless and lossy image compression. The fundamental intention is to give acceptable compression proportion which limits the testing existence intricacy. BAM methods produce better improvement in compression effectiveness without adding any extra usefulness or region overhead. The proposed compression strategies will be looked at with other existing techniques regarding quality. The proposed method is implementing MATLAB 2015 and calculated PSNR, MSE and CR.

articleTitle: Plastic Type Classification for Edge Devices Without Internet
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The management of plastic waste in our ecosystem represents a significant environmental issue, necessitating effective sorting and categorization to facilitate efficient recycling practices. This study introduces a methodology utilizing deep learning for the automated identification of plastic varieties through the application of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) framework. The proposed method of adopting a pre-trained VGG16 to extract the features and tailors them with special layers in order to classify into seven categories that include HDPE, LDPE, Other, PET, PP, PS, and PVC. Data augmentation techniques were used to enhance the functionality of the model; image segmentation enhances object areas visibility. TensorFlow Lite was used to prepare the optimised model for its deployment to mobile platforms for real-time classifying different types of plastics on mobile devices. The optimization of mobile technology boosts the segregation of plastics at the origin, thereby allowing individuals to make informed choices in the recycling process and boosting recycling effectiveness through early differentiation. This approach generates great potential for alleviating environmental impacts through decentralized source-based plastic sorting and waste management.

articleTitle: Analysis of Lidar Signal Noise Reduction in Power Spectrum Density (PSD) estimation using Filters
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper designs and compares three different filtering methods to reduce the effects of noise in power density lidar signal such as Raleigh and Mie scattering refers primarily to the elastic scattering of light. The low pass filter excludes the noise at a low-level, moving average filter takes average values of the signal, wiener filtering adapts to the local noise level and can be effective in reducing noise while preserving signal features and decompose the signal using wavelet transforms and then apply thresholding to remove noise. Simulation results reveal that the Wiener filter appears to be the most effective method for this particular signal and noise scenario. It not only improved the SNR but did so substantially. Both moving average filtering and wavelet denoising showed poorer performance in terms of SNR. This could be due to inappropriate parameter settings or inherent limitations in handling the specific noise characteristics of the signal.

articleTitle: Sign Language Recognition with Image Processing using Deep Learning LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In contemporary society, effective communication remains a cornerstone of human interaction. However, bridging the communication gap presents significant challenges for individuals who are mute or unable to communicate through conventional means, such as sign language. This paper proposes a novel solution leveraging the power of Deep Learning (DL) techniques, specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, to address this issue. Our approach focuses on predicting and detecting actions performed by mute individuals based on sequential frames of interactions. This innovative application of DL and LSTM technologies not only provides a practical solution for overcoming communication barriers but also contributes to advancing inclusive technologies. Through meticulous analysis and training, the DL-LSTM model achieves an impressive 98% accuracy in both action prediction and detection. This work underscores the transformative potential of artificial intelligence in facilitating empathetic and inclusive communication practices, ultimately enriching the fabric of human connection in diverse societal contexts.

articleTitle: Optimized tuberculosis image classification in chest X-rays using transfer learning and hyper parameters
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Timely and accurate detection of tuberculosis (TB) is crucial, as it remains a significant global health concern. In 2023, an estimated 10 million new TB cases were recorded, with 9.8 million affecting adults and 0.2 million children. Tragically, TB was responsible for approximately 1.5 million deaths worldwide, highlighting the need for advanced diagnostic tools. This research focuses on developing a reliable TB classification model using chest X-ray images, employing deep learning methods such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The methodology integrates transfer learning and hyper parameter tuning for improved performance. The dataset comprises 4200 images, including 3500 normal cases and 700 TB-positive cases, sourced from Kaggle's "Tuberculosis (TB) Chest X-ray Database." Leveraging the pre-trained VGG19 architecture, the model utilizes transfer learning techniques, task-specific layer adjustments, regularization methods, and layer freezing for precise classification. The proposed approach achieves an impressive accuracy of 98%, with detailed analysis addressing potential limitations despite its strong performance.

articleTitle: Management of distribution system voltage using solar inverter-a case study of rural feeder
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper explores how advanced solar inverters can enhance grid reliability by managing reactive power, a function traditionally handled by mechanical devices like OLTCs and capacitors. As renewable integration grows, dependency on these conventional methods is less practical due to slower response times and maintenance issues. By adjusting inverter power factor (PF) settings, solar inverters can supply both active and reactive power, contributing to voltage stability. This study models a rural feeder with mixed loads and simulates voltage regulation at 11kV and 33kV levels on ETAP software under different loading conditions and tap settings. Results highlight the potential of solar inverters operating at PFs other than unity to reduce voltage drops and enhance system efficiency. Findings emphasize how tailored PF settings, allow solar inverters to stabilize voltage at distribution levels, thus supporting sustainable grid integration)

articleTitle: Design of Resonant Converter for Light Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Because of their effectiveness and performance, resonant converters are becoming more and more common in DC-DC converter applications for the electric car sector. Every resonant converter topology has a unique set of drawbacks, especially when there are large load fluctuations and light load conditions. A hybrid topology that combines parallel and series configurations has been offered as a solution to these issues. Among the many benefits of the LLC resonant converter are its great proficiency, versatility, and smooth exchanging. Both constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) charging methods frequently use this arrangement. The use of the LLC resonant converter in light electric car charging systems is examined in this article. To test its performance, a 360 W MATLAB simulation was run. According to the findings, the LLC converter efficiently charges the battery by providing a steady 6 A current and 60 V voltage.

articleTitle: SEP Activated GoogLeNet Architecture for Electronic Device Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The research paper presents a tailored GoogLeNet architecture with a novel SEP activation function for image classification tasks in the electronic devices domain. The model incorporates a refined Inception module and undergoes extensive preprocessing for improved feature extraction. The performance evaluation, conducted on a dataset of 1607 electronic device images (resistors, capacitors, transistors, pulse-generators, multi-meters, LEDs, potentiometers, fuses, ICs and breadboards), showcases the model's proficiency in classifying diverse categories of electronic devices. The model architecture, commencing with a 7x7 convolutional layer and progressing through max-pooling, 1x1 convolutions, and custom Inception modules, culminates in an output layer yielding class probabilities. The model achieved an accuracy of 93.04%.

articleTitle: Design of Low Power TG Based FinFET D-Flip Flop for Memory Cell Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This article presents innovative research with regard to the design and analysis of a low-power transmission gate-based D-flip-flop circuit with implementation using FinFET technology. The proposed design will improve power efficiency and reduce leakage power, then the existing designs. The design is investigated for several parameters such as static power, dynamic power, and average power, giving importance to improved energy efficiency as well as maintaining steady operation at high frequencies. Simulation studies show that the TG-based FinFET D-flip flop performs better and saves a considerable amount of power, making it suitable for memory cell designs in contemporary energy-constrained applications. When compared to conventional designs, the TG based FinFET D-flip-flop topology significantly decreased circuit average power consumption by up to 9.36%. This work shows the viability of FinFETs in future designs of low-power, high-performance memories and provides design trade-off information.

articleTitle: Assistance for Visually Impaired individuals using Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: People with Visual Impairments are vulnerable to various challenges in their everyday lives ranging from Access to Information, Travelling to places, Recognizing their surroundings, Isolated Lifestyle and much more. The Proposed solution aims to address these socially inclusive problems through the use of Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning and Computer Vision. The feature index involves using Object Detection models like Yolo v5 for Obstacle avoidance, Integration of Google Map API for Seamless Navigation and NLP based Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for Text Recognition. An average accuracy of 86 percentage was achieved across all models. This solution aims to provide Better Lifestyle, Increased accessibility and Reduced Dependability for the Community of Visually Impaired Individuals.

articleTitle: Analysis of CAD tools in VLSI Physical design
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The increasing complexity of VLSI physical design has elevated the need for advanced CAD tools capable of efficiently managing tasks such as floor planning, placement, routing, and optimization. This study presents a detailed evaluation of prominent CAD tools, analyzing their effectiveness in addressing the critical demands of modern VLSI design, including power efficiency, performance, and scalability. By comparing the strengths and limitations of each tool, this work aims to guide practitioners in selecting optimal solutions for their specific design requirements. Additionally, emerging trends in CAD development, particularly the integration of AI and machine learning, are discussed as pathways to further enhance design automation. Our analysis provides insights that not only underscore the current capabilities of CAD tools but also suggest directions for future research to meet the evolving needs of the VLSI industry.

articleTitle: A Secure Message Encoding & Decoding Method Using Images
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Secure and reliable information transfer is very important in present scenario. Hackers steal the messages by launching plenty of security attacks and make the entire information system unreliable. In the present communication, a text encoding/decoding method is proposed which can be very useful for transmitting messages in a secure and reliable manner. A user can encode any text message (which is to be transmitted) into an image and forward it to the recipient. On their end, the recipient can interpret it, enabling communication in this manner keeping the message hidden to the hackers. The proposed method is effective and easy to implement in day-to-day data communication.

articleTitle: A Review Analysis – RO Waste Water Management System with Home Automation using Green Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Reverse Osmosis (RO) is a traditional technique for filtering water, especially for drinking purpose. Around 75% of contaminated water gets discharged as waste. The principal goal of this paper is to make a seamless system to manage the reusage of the effluent water where the user can get the real time feedback. The proposed system is integrated with ESP32 uses Bluetooth Low Energy and Wi-Fi (802.11 b/g/n) protocols to communicate devices with ESP RainMaker application. The RainMaker provides user the interface to control nodes and monitor data from diverse nodes, using HTTP/HTTPS or MQTT protocols. Initially an effluent water is stored in a common tank. The water level indicator is installed into a tank to monitor the level of water. A custom 12-channel (Single Pole double throw (SPDT)) relay module is connected to diverse household devices such as an electric bulb, fan, switch and solenoid valve. Once the water crosses the level the sensor will send the data and the pump turns on allowing user to manually control the on/off positions. Powered by solar energy, the system offers an eco-friendly solution by utilizing a solar-charged power bank. This setup presents a sustainable and energy-efficient approach to both water conservation and home automation.

articleTitle: Implementation of Baugh-Wooley Multiplier Using Hybrid Full Adder
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The majority of the most recent data-driven advancements, notably artificial-intelligence (AI) and machine-learning (ML) depend heavily on binary arithmetic computations. This paper focuses on the design and analysis of a reliable, low-power 4-bit Baugh- Wooley (BW) multiplier employing the high-performance Hybrid full adder using XOR-XNOR cell. The effectiveness of the proposed 4-bit BW multiplier is thoroughly investigated for power and delay parameters at different operating voltages. The proposed 4-bit BW multiplier at a CMOS process employing a hybrid full adder circuit consumes a minimal power of 303.1 nW at an operating voltage of 1 V. The power consumption increases linearly with operating voltage for the designed BW multiplier employing the high performance full- adder circuits. The proposed 4-bit BW multiplier has a delay of 3.91 ps at 1 V. The simulation result analysis indicates the combination of XOR-XNOR cell in the design of low-power 4-bit Baugh-Wooley multipliers.

articleTitle: FPGA-Implemented Reconfigurable Logic Locking Using N-Stage Delays for Obfuscation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: System security is becoming an increasingly essential feature of modern computing systems, particularly programmable hardware such as Field Programmable Gate arrays (FPGA), employed in various applications such as autonomous systems and digital networks. However, safeguarding FPGA-based devices against IP theft and reverse engineering is difficult and a big concern for the semiconductor and defense industries. Previously, various obfuscation approaches such as gate level obfuscation, camouflaging, and strong puff were employed to make a distinct key for every chip. These designs, however, are more area-intensive, consume more power, and are easier to crack the key. In this research, we propose a novel obfuscation idea that integrates a reconfigurable hardware obfuscation block into the original circuit with an additional N-stage Delay circuit to enhance overall system security and resistance to threats. The present idea relates to the increase in the security of the system against the piracy, overbuilding and from the cloning and camouflaging of the chip. The proposed technique does not have any bulky circuit, and it is easily realizable and just requires some additional modules that can easily reconfigured with a very smaller area and power overhead thereby offering performance benefits and increasing the time of sat attack iteration, making the locking system more complex and difficult to decode.

articleTitle: Plant Leaf Disease Detection Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: For the Indian economy to meet the demands of its people and improve the welfare of its farmers, agricultural output is crucial. Crop diseases and pests can significantly lower yield and quality, making increased crop output impossible. Recognizing these problems is critical to precision agriculture operations. Crop leaves and other plant parts can be examined using deep learning to identify diseases and pests. This work looks into deep learning approaches for detecting illnesses and pests in crops and presents a model for automated diagnosis. Farmers must be able to diagnose agricultural illnesses and pests in order to prevent crop harm. An overview of crop disease and pest diagnosis techniques is provided in this abstract. Usually, visual inspection and clues like discolored, wilting, or irregular leaves are used to identify crops. Agronomists and farmers utilize their expertise to recognize pests and illnesses unique to a given crop. But this tactic is arbitrary and liable to be wrong. To address these issues and enhance the effectiveness and precision of identification, cutting-edge technologies have been developed.

articleTitle: Advanced Photonic Crystal Fiber Sensor Design For Efficient Air Pollution Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for air pollution monitoring using Photonic Crystal Fiber (PCF) with unique optical properties. Through Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations in COMSOL, the study explores how the PCF’s guiding characteristics are influenced by its geometric parameters at different wavelengths. The sensor, designed for enhanced sensitivity, selectivity, and fast response, focuses on detecting air pollutants. A microstructured core in the PCF enhances light-matter interaction, improving sensor performance. The optimized PCF structure ensures effective light confinement, enabling precise detection of environmental changes like temperature and refractive index variations. The results have significant potential for telecommunications, biomedicine, and environmental monitoring applications, contributing to advanced air pollution control technologies.

articleTitle: Low Power SRAM Cell Design for Data Logging Application
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The improved low-power 8-transistor (8T) SRAM cell discussed in this work is intended for data logging applications. This cell was designed using a transmission gate-grounded technique, which considerably lower power consumption compared to more traditional designs. The cell uses as little as 2.63 microwatts when using 180nm technology. The Cadence Virtuoso tool was used to simulate the design's performance. In addition to providing high-speed read and write operation, essential for data logging applications, the 8T configuration improves data retention stability and efficiency. Low-power applications that consider energy economy can benefit from this enhanced SRAM architecture.

articleTitle: Secure Chip To Chip Communication Based On Zero Trust Architecture In Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Nowadays, semiconductor companies frequently outsource the production of chips to meet the rising demand for integrated circuits. As a result, the chip supply chain is now dealing with a number of security problems, like hardware intellectual property theft, trojans, and over-production. In critical systems where adversary assaults have the potential to cause large losses or damage, zero-trust offers a promising method for guaranteeing the validity of Integrated Circuits (ICs). A reliable protocol which makes use of certificates to guarantee the legitimacy of ICs is the Security Protocol and Data Model (SPDM). The work under this study presents a secure chip-to-chip (S2C) zero-trust security architecture based on SPDM protocol, which attempts to authenticate any attached peripheral before using it. The contributions include a comprehensive explanation of the proposed design, the SPDM protocol's implementation, and a discussion of the obstacles that were encountered while executing and implementing.

articleTitle: Flood Risk Assessment of Bihar State of India using Sentinel-1 on Google Earth Engine
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The devastating impact of floods could result in long-term economic consequences, property damage, mortality, and disruptions to essential services. Flood risk assessment is crucial to the solution of these problems because it provides valuable information about the potential frequency and magnitude of flooding episodes. Through a rigorous examination of variables such as geography, hydrology, land use, and climatic changes, flood risk assessment determines how susceptible populations and assets are to flooding. This method assists in locating areas that are vulnerable to flooding. With this information at hand, policymakers may improve catastrophe planning and response procedures, create informed plans for reducing the effects of floods, and allocate resources more effectively to reduce their effects. In the proposed method, the otsu and difference thresholding methods are being used to calculate the population affected by the flood. The model is 92.3% accurate in predicting the locations of the 12 affected districts. The resulting flood map may then be coupled with demographic statistics.

articleTitle: A Grid-Connected 30 kW 5-Level Bidirectional Multilevel Converter for Electric Vehicle Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper focuses on bidirectional power flow and its control in a single-phase grid-connected Electric Vehicle Charging System (EVCS). Bidirectional power flow allows the EV battery to either store energy or send it to the utility grid when needed. This is possible through a bidirectional converter between the grid and the EV battery. While 3-level converters are commonly used for this purpose, they can impose significant stress on the switches during high-power charging. To address this issue, this study explores the use of a 5-L bidirectional Active Neutral Point Clamped (ANPC) converter for high-powered off-board EV charging systems. For effective power flow control, Phase Locked Loops (PLLs) are critical. The Second Order Generalized Integrator (SOGI) PLL is particularly effective for maintaining stability and ensuring good performance under dynamic conditions. In this research, the SOGI PLL is employed to control the grid current, and the ANPC converter is evaluated. The suggested model is implemented in MATLAB platform to validate its stability.

articleTitle: Real-Time Performance Assessment of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations with RTDS
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In this study, author discussed about prospects and tasks for power grid integration with electric vehicle (EVs) and real-time analysis of EV charging and discharging EVs stations performed on the RTDS. It aims to evaluate the characteristics of EV charging/discharging, power flow and state of charge (SoC) of EVs in grid-connected modes. By modelling various scenarios including different levels of EV penetration, charging patterns and grid conditions, the analysis offers insights into the dynamic behaviour of the system. The real time digital simulator (RTDS) environment enables high-fidelity simulation of power system components and real-time control strategies facilitating a detailed examination of voltage stability, frequency regulation and load control. The results highlight the potential of advanced control strategies such as hybrid PSO-GA algorithms to determine optimum result by derived specialized method to maximize and minimize objective function.

articleTitle: Question Pair Similarity Detection and Development of Question Answering Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The development of a question-answer chatbot involves leveraging advanced embedding techniques to optimize language understanding and response generation. The process begins with curating a diverse dataset of questions and answers, followed by preprocessing steps such as tokenization, stemming, and stop-word removal. Various embedding techniques, including traditional methods like BoW and TF-IDF, as well as modern approaches such as Word2Vec, GloVe, and BERT, are explored to determine the most effective technique for chatbot optimization. Performance metrics such as accuracy, responsiveness, and scalability guide the evaluation process. The approach encompasses data collection, preprocessing, embedding, model training, and user interaction, aiming to enhance human-computer interactions and improve information retrieval.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Matrix Converter based Versatile Wireless Power Flow System for G2V and V2X Operation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: A Bidirectional Matrix Converter (BMC)-based wireless power flow system is proposed for a versatile Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) operation. The system integrates advanced power electronic converters with Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technology to enable seamless two-way energy transfer between electric. vehicles (EVs) and the .grid, as well as between vehicles and various loads in the surrounding environment. The matrix converter, capable of handling both AC and DC inputs, uses bidirectional switches to enable two-way power flow. The BMC acts as a key enabler for efficient bidirectional power conversion, offering high power quality, compact design, and reduced losses in both charging and discharging modes. To verify its suitability, the converter's performance was simulated in MATLAB/Simulink with specified design parameters, followed by experimental validation using a 3.3 kW laboratory prototype. The results demonstrated high-efficiency power conversion and reliable bidirectional power flow, aligning closely between simulation and experiment. This system shows promise as an environmentally friendly and efficient solution for wireless EV charging applications, advancing the development of sustainable EV infrastructure.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Speed Control Techniques for PMSM using in EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: When it comes to Field-Oriented Control (FOC) drives for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs), Proportional-Integral (PI) controllers are steadily the default. When challenged with sudden variations in load, PI controllers exhibit a lengthy settling time and a large early stage overrun. Intelligent algorithm such as Artificial Neural Network (ANN)enhance the performance of conventional PI. This study analyzes two distinct controllers (ANN and PI) with FOC-based drive Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) controlled PMSM drive speed control, regardless the fact that ANN executes system changes faster and enhances performance to the required level. Both controllers' rising, settling, peak, and peak overshoot times were tested in a MATLAB/Simulink simulation of the whole system model. The simulation results are displayed and analyzed for all PMSM drives that are based on speed controllers. The simulation results clearly show that, in terms of speed responses, the ANN controller performs better than the PI-based controller.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Hand Exoskeleton for Rheumatoid Arthritis Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Inflammation of the joints is a hallmark of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a long-term inflammatory disease that can cause significant discomfort, limited range of motion, and impaired hand function. Developing a tailored hand exoskeleton to help RA patients carry out routine activities and regain some dexterity in their hands is the primary goal of this study. This exoskeleton is designed specifically for RA sufferers. It uses precise actuation technology and soft, adaptable materials to help in gripping and finger extension without making the patient uncomfortable or requiring them to move against their will. With its built-in sensors, the exoskeleton keeps tabs on the user's every motion, analyzing their joint locations and patterns to provide real-time feedback and tailor adjustments to their specific mobility and pain. RA sufferers will be able to modify the support levels of the exoskeleton based on the type of activity they are performing and the amount of pain they are experiencing. Control will be achieved through an interface that is easy to use. This project aims to produce an assistive device that improves the quality of life for individuals with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) by boosting freedom in daily activities while minimizing joint stress. This will be accomplished by merging several biomedical principles with modern robotics.

articleTitle: Optimization and Control of Photovoltaic Power Generation System Connected to the Utility Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This research dives into the design of a solar energy system that can generate electricity and supply it for both household appliances and the power grid. To maximize the power output from the solar panels, the system implements a special control technique called Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT). The MPPT technique utilizes an algorithm called Incremental Conductance to achieve this. Before the inverter stage, a boost converter is incorporated to elevate the voltage from the solar panels further. The inverter itself plays a critical role in seamlessly integrating solar energy into the power grid. It employs a complex synchronization method known as synchronous reference frame control. To thoroughly assess the system's performance under various operating conditions, the researchers modelled and simulated the entire system using MATLAB/Simulink software. This software allows them to test the system's behavior and fine-tune its operation for optimal efficiency and grid integration

articleTitle: EEG-Based Epileptic Detection Using Hybrid Convolutional-LSTM Model And Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Epileptic seizure detection is one of the critical tasks in healthcare monitoring. These epileptic seizures occur because of unusual electrical impulses in the brain and can vary in seriousness, duration, and type. Many methods and procedures have been suggested for this automatic epilepsy seizure signals detection using AI and deep neural networks. With the help of an attention mechanism, this study introduces a novel hybrid deep learning framework that combines long short-term memory networks (LSTMs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Electroencephalogram (EEG) data can be effectively analyzed by the suggested model to identify patterns in both space and time, enabling robust seizure detection. In this model, CNNs capture spatial patterns, while LSTMs capture temporal patterns. The methodology involves Dynamic temporal pooling and channel-based attention mechanisms to further refine feature extraction and improve model performance. An ensemble of multiple models is employed to enhance robustness and generalization.The proposed method achieves 99.40% accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods. This analysis provides interpretability, highlighting key EEG features contributing to seizure detection. This proposed model grants an encouraging solution for advancing the detection and control of epilepsy.

articleTitle: Smart Classroom Power Automation: An Adaptive And Predictive Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The growing demand for energy efficiency in educational institutions has led to the exploration of smart technologies for managing power consumption. This project introduces a "Power Automation for Classrooms" system that leverages long-range RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) technology to automate the activation of classroom lights and fans based on student attendance. The system operates by detecting student entries through RFID tags without the need for manual scanning, thus ensuring a seamless and instant process. The project aims to reduce energy wastage by activating the power in stages depending on the number of students present, with specific power allocation thresholds set according to the class strength. The data on students entered, as well as the power consumption for each classroom, is stored in the cloud, allowing for real-time monitoring, analysis and supports data-driven decision-making for future energy planning.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in 5G Cellular Networks Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Along with the advancement of telecommunications, 5G networks have become the backbone of modern broadband cellular networks which offers high-speed data. This article shows a method based on Machine Learning (ML) for Network Anomaly Detection (NAD) in 5G communication, focusing to identify unusual or potentially harmful behaviours in real time.
