Given the complexity and high volume of 5G traffic, we explore various algorithms for effective anomaly detection, including Autoencoders, One-Class SVM, Random Forest, and two ensemble approaches. The dataset used for this study is a cellular dataset representing typical 5G traffic patterns. We implement two ensemble techniques to enhance prediction robustness: Ensemble 1 (Voting Classifier with AdaBoost, Decision Tree, and Gradient Boosting) and Ensemble 2 (Voting Classifier with AdaBoost, Decision Tree, and ExtraTree). Ensemble 2 achieves the highest accuracy at 100%, demonstrating its effectiveness in anomaly detection for 5G networks.

articleTitle: A Multi-Feature Analysis of Electric Vehicle Performance Using Statistical Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: As electric vehicles (EVs) gain wider acceptance, a data-driven understanding of their performance efficiency becomes increasingly essential. This study investigates whether data regarding EVs can be effectively measured using data science, focusing on key parameters. A comprehensive multi-feature dataset was nalysed using various statistical methods, including Shapiro-Wilk tests for normality, exploratory data analysis (EDA), and correlation analysis. The analysis revealed non-normal distributions for several performance metrics. In contrast, Charging Time (Hours) and Weight (Kg) were found to be normally distributed. Summary statistics highlighted significant variability in variables like Range with a mean of 338.79 km. Correlation matrices unveiled critical relationships between attributes. This paper provides insights into key EV performance factors, supporting optimization and informed decision-making.

articleTitle: Facial and Ocular-Based Cattle Biometric Recognition Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Biometric recognition of cattle will be one of the most effective ways of improving livestock management, controlling diseases, and breeding. Traditional methods, such as ear tagging, are invasive, prone to errors, and lost or even tampered with. This paper proposes a biometric recognition system for cattle using facial and ocular features as signatures to identify individual cattle using DNN. It utilizes state-of-the-art CNNs to extract and analyze features from cattle faces and eyes to deliver accurate identification. The use of biometric markers like muzzle patterns, the structure of the eye, and symmetry for meaningful characterization provides an alternative approach to traditional methods that are non-invasive and reliable. Deep learning-based model training on a diverse training dataset of cattle images enables the network to learn robust features that generalize well across different breeds and environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Precision Land Use and Land Cover Mapping with a High-Accuracy Time Series LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper introduces a machine-learning-based LULC classifying model developed with a time series data set, trained on a diverse set of agriculture and non-agricultural classes. It used a strong generalization capability employing an LSTM architecture; that is, it achieved accuracy of 90.04% in training and also validation accuracy of 90.55%. The ultimate accuracy was obtained at the minimal loss of 0.1909 at the accuracy of 95.58%, thereby validating its usability for LULC pattern classification. This model has a wide-range of potential application in environmental monitoring and resource management. Future work involves introducing more variables into the dataset, the inclusion of other environmental factors, and fine-tuning of the model towards more general applications in geospatial applications. Thus, this work advances the current state of remote sensing and LULC classification to present an effective tool in sustainable land management.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of BD-EMD-IMFs Fusion Based Features Extraction and Classification for Glaucoma Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: There are various disorders in the human eye. Glaucoma is considered to be one of the most severe eye disorders. It develops with very less speed in the eye and damages all the optic nerves present inside the eyes. The outdated glaucoma prediction methods are more costly and slow. A better work about glaucoma prediction using fused bi-dimensional empirical mode decomposition- intrinsic mode functions-based feature extraction and classification from the fundus image is presented here. BD-EMD-IMFs are obtained from the preprocessed color components. Fused BD-EMD-IMFs based features extraction is the key idea of this work. Fused BD-EMD-IMFs-Based features are then normalized and classified with support vector machines (SVM). The pooled feature accuracy (Acc) reached 97.2 with 10-fold cross-validation (FCV). The experimental analysis clearly brings out the superiority of the proposed method over the traditional.

articleTitle: Arrhythmia Classification using Scalogram-based EfficientNet
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Classification of arrhythmia from electrocardiogram (ECG) is vital in accurately diagnosing cardiac disorders. In the proposed work, the developed model classifies seven cardiac arrhythmia classes using the pre-trained EfficientNet B5 convolutional neural network (CNN). The model was trained by continuous wavelet transform images, which transformed the one-dimensional ECG signals into two-dimensional scalogram images. With this, the proposed model reached an accuracy of 99.11%, 97.90% precision, 97.73% recall, and 97.81% F-Score when tested against the open-source MIT-BIH arrhythmia database. Results are compared with EfficientNet B1. EfficientNet B5 and CWT integration enhanced the performance over the most advanced methods for classifying ECG arrhythmia.

articleTitle: Wideband SIW antenna for mm-wave band of 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Antennas are more effective and useful when they have higher gain along with better efficiency over a larger frequency range. To fulfil this, wide band U type slotted substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna is designed in the context of 5G communications. In this work, a slotted SIW antenna is designed and developed for 5G, which has the frequency bands 26.50 – 29.50 GHz (n257) and 27.5 – 28.35 GHz (n261). The proposed antenna is made using RT-duroid as the substrate material with a relative permittivity ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 2.2 and height of 0.787 mm. The designed antenna has a peak gain of 7.2 dB, 3.2 GHz bandwidth, which is nearly 11.5% of the center frequency. To increase the impedance bandwidth, two shorting vias are positioned beneath the U-shaped slot, which are engraved into the patch. The antenna displays resonant frequency at 27.5 GHz. The antenna specifications such as radiation patterns, gain and reflection coefficient are used to describe efficient performance of the antenna.

articleTitle: Analysis of Soiling Impacts on 100 kWp Rooftop Solar PV Plant
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper gives a comprehensive analysis of the impact of soiling on the performance of a 100 kWP rooftop photovoltaic (PV) plant using a 2.5-year dataset from NIT Trichy. Traditional soiling measurement methods often rely on specialized equipment, which can limit their accessibility and scalability. This study eliminates the need for special sensors by using historical and real-time operational data, such as irradiance, panel temperature, and power output. Seasonal patterns in soiling losses are thus revealed, allowing optimization of cleaning schedules to maintain energy output at expected levels. Notably, the analysis shows that 34.2% of the plant's capacity remains unutilized due to soiling. This work contributes to the design of robust PV maintenance strategies by demonstrating a scalable data-driven approach to soiling assessment, making it specifically suitable for medium-sized installations.

articleTitle: Laser Triangulation and Optical Computed Tomography 3D Scanner
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: 3D scanning encounters challenges when scanning objects with complex optical properties, such as translucency. To address the issue, the research developed an improved 3D scanner by integrating Laser Triangulation with Optical Computed Tomography (OPCT). The prototype was tested on various object shapes and sizes, and its accuracy was evaluated using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD). The results demonstrated an overall accuracy of 95.85%, with consistent point cloud generation when proper calibration was maintained. While the prototype had an average scan duration 28.43% longer than that of an industrial scanner, its integrated scanning technique provided reliable performance for both opaque and translucent objects. The findings underscore the potential of combining Laser Triangulation and OPCT to create a versatile and effective 3D scanning solution for objects with complex optical properties.

articleTitle: Design of a M-shaped microstrip patch antenna for ISM band of applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: A micro-strip patch antenna (MPA) is widely applied in the field of wireless communication, due to its smaller size and frequency of operation. An M-shaped MPA is proposed in this paper which operates in the band of 2.4GHz. The rectangular MPA has many slot shapes or strips, such as M-Strip, Zigzag pattern, and multiple circles, to enhance properties like VSWR, return loss(RL), gain, and frequency bandwidth. Microstrip patch antennas are becoming more and more popular because of their small, flat shape. These antennas can be readily applied in spacecraft, airplanes or portable communication devices. This antenna design's VSWR and return loss at 2.4GHz are measured to be 1.06 and -42.463 dB, respectively. The suggested antenna accomplishes downsizing without sacrificing return loss, VSWR, or resonant frequency by using microstrip line feeding.

articleTitle: Minimization of Harmonic for Grid Connected Hybrid Wind and Solar Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The green energy has become an inevitable source of non-polluting electrical energy generation. In order to reduce the amount of environmental pollution and to improve the economic development, the hybrid wind and solar system is nowadays preferred. Wind and solar energy hybrid system has some drawbacks like difficulties in extracting energy with high speed and the availability is different in different areas and in different seasons. Also hybridization reduces the power flow between the sources. Extracting the maximum output from the converters is also another difficult task in this system. Energy has become a crucial part of life and it must be secure and renewable. So automatically the necessity of energy management becomes very important. A bust-boost converter is created and simulated the field of solar and wind energy. The high frequency switch’s gate pulse is managed by using an MPPT algorithm. At 50 Hz frequency, the grid frequency the phase a grid current harmonics have a maximum component present with a 2.31% deviation.

articleTitle: Refining Crop Pest Recognition Performance through Dynamically Adaptable Activation Patterns of Kolmogorov Arnold Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Food contains several nutrients which help in growth and development of the human body, which come from crops. However, Pest infestation can be a big threat due to it causing various types of diseases in crops, reducing crop production. Thus, it is necessary to detect pests early and take steps to stop the infestation. Therefore, in this study, we have proposed a novel model named VGG19-KAN for crop pest detection and compared it with models like Mobilenetv2 and VGG19. VGG19-KAN is a model that replaces the traditional Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifier with a Kolmogorov Arnold Network (KAN), which hypothetically improves the generalization power through dynamically adaptable activation patterns. We used the IP102 dataset, where the pest images are divided into 8 crop categories to train the models. We found that VGG19-KAN performed fairly better than Mobilenetv2 and the base VGG19 with 1-3% accuracy improvement for each crop type, thus proving its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Marine Robot for Underwater Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Underwater surveillance has become a crucial area of research, particularly for marine exploration and environmental monitoring, with marine robots playing a vital role. These robots, equipped with sensors and cameras, capture real-time data and images from underwater environments, reducing the need for human intervention in hazardous areas. However, a major challenge in this field is developing reliable communication networks, as underwater environments face limitations in bandwidth, range, and signal attenuation, hindering real-time data transmission. This paper presents a simple marine robot prototype based on the Raspberry Pi Model 4B, utilizing Electronic Speed Controllers (ESCs) and brushless motors for efficient movement. The robot's body is manually designed using 3D printing technology, with PETG (polyethylene terephthalate glycol) material chosen for its water resistance, durability, and buoyancy. The design ensures the robot’s stability and functionality underwater, offering a cost-effective solution for marine robotics while underscoring the need for improved underwater communication technologies.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Review of Brain Tumor Segmentation and Classification Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Brain tumor segmentation and classification through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are critical yet complex tasks, which usually require extensive manual labor. Both are non-invasive methods and so are a good alternative to biopsy. They have a higher diagnostic accuracy and more concertedly planned treatment than the combined approaches. Since the late 1990s, research has moved from region-growing techniques to traditional machine learning and advanced deep neural networks. These approaches have succeeded in segmenting brain tumors according to their histological type. Consisting of the region-growing method, shallow machine learning and deep learning, the paper also discusses preprocessing, feature selection, post-processing and use of data sets. In addition, taking up all the ideas from previous documents in this volume, we create a meta-analysis which aims to systematically evaluate and compare various machine learning models with quantitative results, suggesting how they might be applied to different types of problems. Finally, this review summarizes the challenges and potential future developments in the field.

articleTitle: A Variable Frequency Switching Scheme for THD Reduction with 13-level Symmetrical Inverter under Test
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: To reduce distortion from the fundamental sinusoidal waveform, inverters were extended to more than two layers, which gave rise to the concept of a multilayer inverter. The need for extra switches, which increases system bulk and cost and decreases system reliability because of the higher component count, is a disadvantage of multiple-level inverters. The distortion in the result is lessened by the increase in inverter levels. In this study, a variety of switching approaches have been tried using a symmetrical 13 level inverter (13-LI) and their results are compared with 180 degree shifted adjacent level pulse span modulation. This is because efficient switching techniques may help minimize distortion. The model and variable switching strategy are constructed using the MATLAB software.

articleTitle: Improvising Language Conversation – Hindi & Urdu
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In a diverse country such as India, natural language processing (NLP) plays an even greater role in resolving the complexities of languages. In this article, we discuss Urdu terminology used by Hindi literature and explain the problem for readers that are not familiar with these phrases. We devised an automated manner to replace Urdu-based words in Hindi sentences with synonymous terms used commonly in conversational or literary Hindi. This study supports current attempts at standardization and simplification that have been underway for Hindi, encouraging linguistic diversification in sectors like the media or education. While there are challenges to solve for, such as handling homonyms and a fixed list of synonyms available, we empirically show strong improvements towards more inclusive language. Overall, the research presents a starting point for future multilingual application-based work and highlights that NLP holds exciting promise to support reliable communication processes within diverse linguistic domains.

articleTitle: Deep ResNet50 Architecture for Enhanced Plant Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Plant disease is a major threat which can lead to economic loss and human loss leading to starvation. This is addressed through timely and accurate detection of these diseases. Traditional methods of disease detection rely heavily on human judgement. To avoid such errors, it’s more feasible to develop an ML-based system, that can minimizes errors and maximize the output. We used ResNet50 architecture for accurate results. The ResNet architecture is a cutting-edge deep neural network. This is the most preferred approach towards deep learning. Here, complicated images are taken into consideration. The vanishing gradient problem is resolved, resulting in better performance. Our study used the PlantVillage dataset with 15 folders of varieties of diseases and their labels. The experimental results were clear, showing that our approach to the model was efficient in detection of the diseases within the plants at an accuracy of 99.71%, outperforming other deep learning models. Levels of accuracy show that the ResNet50 model is a valuable toolbox for agricultural practitioners and researchers.

articleTitle: RFID based Automatic Pathway for Emergency Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This project introduces an automated traffic control system aimed at facilitating the swift movement of emergency vehicles through urban intersections. Leveraging the integration of RFID and IoT technologies, the system utilizes Node MCU and Arduino Mega microcontrollers for seamless communication and traffic management. RFID tags affixed to emergency vehicles trigger dynamic control over traffic signals, ensuring unobstructed passage. Audible alerts through a buzzer and real-time information displayed on an LCD enhance safety and situational awareness. Coordinated LED signals optimize traffic flow, while IoT integration with Adafruit enables remote operation capabilities. Future enhancements, including GPS tracking with the SIM800L module, would support real-time, location-specific traffic adjustments, significantly reducing response times and enhancing the efficiency of city traffic management.

articleTitle: Minimalist Event Coreference with CCNN
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to event coreference resolution focusing on minimalistic features and leveraging Conjoined Convolutional Neural Networks (CCNN). Unlike traditional methods reliant on linguistic and parsing-based features, my system relies solely on lemmatization and precomputed word embeddings, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the ECB+ corpus. I systematically evaluate the effectiveness of commonly used features and introduce a clustering strategy that enhances the robustness of pairwise predictions. my approach demonstrates the efficacy of CCNN in capturing the mentioned similarities and outperforms existing models on within-doc event coreference resolution tasks.

articleTitle: Memristor-Fet Hybrid Circuits for Real-Time Electronic Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Circuits comprising of memristor paired with Field effective transistor (FET) were determined to be exceedingly significant as the output current modulated by the FET heightened memristive executions. In this paper, the memristor-FET pair is studied in terms of its electronic features. The duo exhibited the characteristics of negative resistance. Interestingly, the duo was capable of generating ramp and pulse signals with improved circuit complexity of ~93% when compared to conventional signal generators. Importantly, the linearity was improved by ~20.5%.

articleTitle: Quantum Resistance Blockchain Algorithm using QHF and Novel Consensus Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The emergence of quantum computing poses a significant threat to the security of traditional blockchain systems, which rely heavily on classical cryptographic algorithms. To safeguard the integrity and reliability of blockchain technology in the upcoming era, this work proposes a novel quantum-resistant blockchain architecture. This approach integrates a robust consensus mechanism, with advanced quantum cryptographic primitives, including quantum digital signatures based on a Quantum Hash Function (QHF). Incorporating a quantum hash function enhances the blockchain resistance, providing an additional layer of security against quantum attacks. By combining these elements, our method creates a blockchain system fortified against the potential vulnerabilities introduced by quantum computers. The proposed solution leverages the power of QHFs to safeguard transaction integrity, while the consensus mechanism ensures the reliability and decentralization of the network. This paper also delves into the theoretical underpinnings of quantum blockchains, exploring their design, feasibility, and potential applications, emphasizing their promising future, particularly in areas such as decentralized identity authentication. Finally, it contributes to the development of a secure and resilient blockchain ecosystem capable of thriving in the coming era.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Secondary Protein Structure Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Protein secondary structure prediction is a pivotal task in computational biology, essential for understanding protein folding and function. This study evaluates the efficacy of three models—K-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, and a Transfer Learning-based approach in classifying secondary protein structures. A subset of the RCSB Protein Data Bank was used, with sequences preprocessed using tokenization and padding. To address class imbalance, three oversampling techniques were implemented. Without oversampling, the Transfer Learning model achieved the highest accuracy (77.65%) and Q3 accuracy (66.17%). With oversampling, Transfer Learning maintained robust performance with an accuracy of 77.35% and Q3 accuracy of 65.72%, outperforming KNN and RF models. These results highlight the potential of transfer learning in advancing protein structure prediction, especially when coupled with effective preprocessing techniques.

articleTitle: GPS Based Electronic Toll Collection System with Energy Harvesting Capability
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In this work, we proposed a Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna (RDRA) based Global Positioning System (GPS) antenna with energy harvesting capabilities to replace and eradicate traffic jams at the toll plaza due to existing RFID technology. The GPS-based Electronic Toll with an efficient system is envisioned to streamline toll operations, reduce congestion, and improve the overall user experience with localization capabilities. The L1 band GPS antenna is connected to two channels, one with energy harvesting and another with an onboard unit (OBU) of the electronic system. In this paper, the GPS L1 antenna is designed at 1575.42 MHz. The GPS L1 antenna is designed with a matching circuit and RF to DC voltage devices, such as speed sensors, that can be powered by radio frequency energy harvesting systems used at GPS-based toll plazas.

articleTitle: Price-sensitive Energy Management System for Grid-tied PV-battery-based EV Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: As more consumers prioritize reducing their carbon footprint, EVs offer a cleaner alternative to traditional gasoline vehicles. This paper proposes an Energy management system that is crucial in optimizing the interaction between EVs, the grid, photovoltaic systems, and battery storage. These systems efficiently manage power flow, ensuring that renewable energy is utilized effectively while minimizing costs. By prioritizing charging based on factors like grid demand and energy availability, EMS helps maximize the benefits of both EVs and renewable sources, enhancing overall energy efficiency and supporting a more sustainable energy ecosystem. The proposed EMS is validated for all modes in Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Tawna Yachaq an Intelligent System for the safe movement of people with visual disabilities
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The development of the intelligent system "Tawna Yachaq" is presented for the safe movement of a volunteer with visual disabilities. This system includes a cane with an obstacle detection system, an artificial vision system for the identification of objects and people, with an alert and position warning system in a controlled environment. The mechanical system consists of an intelligent system protection box developed in Fusion 360 software. The electronic-electrical design of the intelligent system, based on the Raspberry Pi 4B microprocessor. Includes a Neo 6M GPS module to provide real-time user location. Using HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensors and a buzzer module, it emits an alert sound to the user. In addition, an ESP32-Cam camera that uses computer vision algorithms detects predefined objects in the university campus environment. The system is powered by 7.4V Lion rechargeable batteries, with an LM2596 voltage regulator ensuring stable operation. A patent is proposed as future work.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Education with PersonifAI: A Deep Dive into AI-Driven Personalized Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents PersonifAI. An education platform, for students powered by artificial intelligence to develop skills in high demand areas such as project management digital marketing and data analysis After an initial evaluation to identify users strengths and weaknesses the platform uses a customized Llama 3.1(8 billion) model to provide personalized audiobooks textbooks curriculum materials and quizzes Through the use of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) PersonifAI guarantees that the content is relevant individualized and responsive, to each user's needsThe study details how artificial intelligence (AI) is set to revolutionize the field of education by offering perspectives on personalized learning in the years and showcases PersonifAI as a prime illustration of AI driven educational advancements.

articleTitle: AI-Based System for Real-Time Yoga Pose Detection and Correction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Although yoga is recognized for its positive effects on both physical and mental health, injuries can occur from improper positioning while practicing. To tackle this issue, I introduce a real-time yoga pose detection and correction system based on AI. This system employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) for categorizing five popular yoga poses Downward Dog, Goddess, Plank, Tree, and Warrior II. An available dataset was utilized and divided into 80% for training and 20% for testing. Methods like resizing, rotating, magnifying, and mirroring images were utilized to improve the model's effectiveness. The camera-based system monitors body movements and gives instant feedback on pose accuracy, being a helpful tool for yoga enthusiasts. The accuracy of the model on the validation set was 87%, with real-time testing confirming effective pose correction. Future efforts will concentrate on enlarging the dataset and backing up more intricate poses.

articleTitle: Development and Analysis of a High-Efficiency T-Type Inverter based 3.7 kW Wireless EV Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance analysis of a T-type inverter optimized for wireless charging applications in electric vehicle (EV) batteries, aiming to enhance efficiency and reduce power losses. Traditional H-bridge inverter-based wireless power transfer (WPT) systems face challenges such as complex circuitry, voltage spikes, switching noise, and losses from switching, which impact overall efficiency. The proposed T-type inverter addresses these issues by improving voltage control and reducing switching losses, resulting in enhanced system efficiency. The system employs a series-series (S-S) compensation technique that provides better transmission control and performance, making it more adaptable to diverse load conditions. This compensation method, combined with optimized alignment tolerance and a high coupling coefficient, allows the system to efficiently use rectangular coils, which generate a more uniform magnetic field and minimize current loss. Designed for a 3.7 kW output at an operating frequency of 85 kHz, the T-type inverter-based WPT system was validated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations and a laboratory prototype. Results demonstrate an efficiency of 95.20% in simulation and 93.248% in hardware testing. Additionally, DC-DC efficiencies achieved are 94.78% in simulation and 96.177% in hardware. This research confirms the potential of T-type inverters in high-efficiency wireless EV charging systems.

articleTitle: Assessing U-Net Architectures for Effective Brain Tumor Segmentation in MRI
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Accurately segmenting brain tumors using MRI scans is essential for diagnosing, treatment planning and monitoring treatment. This research compares several U-Net based architectures, including U-Net DIU-Net, DFP-ResUNet, BU-Net, and SEResU-Net, which are implemented and evaluated using BraTS 2018 dataset. Each model integrates unique enhancements to address challenges in brain tumor segmentation, like vanishing gradients, poor feature extraction, & class imbalance and trained using BraTS 2018 dataset, and their performance is evaluated using Accuracy, Dice score, and IoU score. The comparative analysis reveals that while each model has specific advantages, the SEResU-Net and BU-Net architectures attain the highest performance metrics, especially in segmenting TC and ET regions. This evaluation of U-Net variants segment brain tumor highlights their strengths and limitations, offering key insights for advancing brain imaging research and clinical.

articleTitle: Analysis of Rotor Flux Barriers in SynRM for Performance Enhancement in Traction Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The growing demand for traction motors has significantly risen in recent years, driven by the limitations and environmental drawbacks of internal combustion (IC) engines. These engines consume high amounts of fossil fuels and emit harmful greenhouse gases, contributing to global environmental concerns. Consequently, the development of efficient, sustainable, and cost-effective electric motors has become crucial to improving vehicle performance and reducing ecological impacts. Among the innovative alternatives, the synchronous reluctance motor (SynRM) has emerged as a promising solution for traction applications, thanks to its compact design, robust construction, high efficiency, and relatively lower production costs. Unlike traditional induction motors and permanent magnet motors, the SynRM eliminates the dependency on magnets, offering economic advantages while promoting environmental sustainability by avoiding rare earth materials. However, the existing SynRM designs often suffer from drawbacks such as excessive torque ripple, low power factor, and inefficient rotor barrier configurations. This project focuses on designing an optimized hyperbolic-polyline flux barrier rotor structure for SynRM to address these challenges. Finite element analysis (FEA) was performed using Ansys Electronic Desktop Student software to evaluate the new design. The simulation results verified that the improved rotor structure significantly reduces torque ripple and enhances the power factor, making it a highly efficient choice for modern electric drive applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Multimodal Transformer Approach for Targeted Information Retrieval from Obscure Images
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Extracting specific information from diverse and complex image types is a challenging task, especially in real-world cases where images often contain noise, low resolution, occlusion, or poor contrast. Traditional approaches struggle in this case as they rely heavily on clear, high-quality datasets, making them unsuitable for cluttered or ambiguous inputs. In this paper, we introduce a novel solution leveraging the Qwen2 multimodal transformer, fine-tuned with the Llama Factory framework, to address these limitations. This approach has practical applications such as extracting product details for e-commerce platforms to improve filters and product detail pages, and retrieving key information from medicine packaging to ensure accurate assortment and categorization. Evaluated on a large dataset with thousands of unique samples, our method shows significant improvements in accurately retrieving information from complex images. The results highlight the robustness and efficiency of our approach, setting a new benchmark for real-world image retrieval tasks.

articleTitle: Designing of Model for Millet Crop Production Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The IoT-powered Millet Crop Production Monitoring System aims to revolutionize millet farming by providing a comprehensive, up-to-date monitoring solution. It integrates IoT devices like sensors and actuators with a centralized platform to collect critical data on temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and crop growth stages. This information helps farmers make informed decisions about fertilization, irrigation, and pest control, optimizing resource use and boosting yields. The system also incorporates predictive analytics using machine learning to anticipate problems and recommend preventive measures. A user-friendly mobile app provides real-time data and alerts, enabling timely action. By addressing issues like limited resources and climate variability, this IoT-based approach promotes sustainable agriculture. Ultimately, it enhances food security and improves the economic well-being of farmers by making millet farming more efficient and precise.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer Technique for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Establishing a green and healthy ecosystem necessitates the reduction of carbon emissions, achievable by decreasing reliance on non-renewable source of energy base vehicles due to the same reason the technology is transfer to electric vehicles (EVs). The EVs can be charge in two modes i.e. dynamically or by means of static charging techniques. In the later mode, fully charged electric vehicles cannot go significant distances. To enhance its range, additional batteries will be required. The potential electric vehicles have to utilize dynamic wireless charging to extend their range and reduce the requirement for substantial battery packs. In this work different WPT techniques are compared and the design of transmitter coils for dynamic WPT. Receiver coils and the transmitter air-gap influences the coupling coefficient and the mutual inductance, which is denoted. During the motion electric vehicle speed and misalignment impact the dynamic WPT system, which is also examined. This document was included. MATLAB/SIMULINK software is used to model and simulate with 10KWh battery pack in dynamic WPT system for power transfer calculation in EV’s.

articleTitle: Design of Hybrid Photo-Voltaic Array Reconfiguration for Dynamic Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The efficiency of the photo-voltaic module decreases substantially when partial and dynamic shading situations arise in solar-generated power systems. Various configuration strategies are commonly utilised to improve performance in PV modules and to eliminate effects of partial shading. Six different shading patterns employing a 7*7 array structure are used to illustrate the hybrid array topologies i.e. HoneyComb-TotalCrossTied (hctct), SeriesParallel-TotalCrossTied (sptct), BridgeLinked-TotalCrossTied (bl-tct), and BridgeLinked-HoneyComb (bl-hc). The performance is considered on basis of, Global maximum power (GMP), mismatch losses (ML), fill factor (FF) and local maximum power point (LMP). 1Soltech 1STH-215-P, PV array structure is modelled and simulated using the MATLAB/Simulink software.

articleTitle: Advancements Of Quantum Dot Cellular Automata: A Comprehensive Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Classical computing technologies face challenges in terms of area, cell count, power, and latency, making it difficult to design faster, and energy efficient systems. Quantum Cellular Automata (QCA) is the promising solution to overcome this problem. This paper provides an extensive review of QCA technology, immersing on various circuit designs and methodologies proposed in recent years.QCA functions by deploying the position of electrons within quantum cells, which allows for binary logic without electric current flow, reducing power consumption. Moreover, QCA requires smaller cell size, and fewer logic gates, unlike CMOS. Furthermore, due to its quantum-based interactions, it reduces latency in processing operations.This paper, summarizes the performance of QCA circuits such as AND Gate, OR Gate, NOT Gate, Majority Gate, 2 input XOR Gate, 3 input XOR Gate, 3 input XNOR Gate, 2 bit Binary to Gray code converter, 5 bit parity generator, Full adder, Full subtractor, Comparator, De-multiplexer proposed in various research articles. Based on the valuable insights from the comprehensive survey, the future scope of QCA is also discussed.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Energy: Reducing Interface Defect Density in PCBM/CH3NH3PbI3/AgSCN Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The aim of this work is to establish the impact of density of interface defects on the performance of PCBM/CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/AgSCN based perovskite solar cells. The aim of this research is to guarantee that everyone has access to dependable, ecologically friendly, reasonably priced energy relevant in the modern day. This aim is in line with Sustainable Development, which holds that access to energy should be globally accessible. It investigate many fundamental photovoltaic metrics including the PCE, the FF, the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>, and the J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>. These characteristics are affected by the higher recombination of charge carriers resulting from a high interface defect density; therefore, the ultimate decline in the overall efficiency of energy conversion at the end of the day. Conversely, reducing the defect density results in an increase in charge transfer, which improves interface quality and thus PCE. Moreover, the improvement of charge transfer results in V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>, FF all experiencing gains. The findings of this work clarify the need of defect control and material optimization in the process of improving the technology underlying perovskite solar cells of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>:- 0.96V, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf> :- 21.3 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, FF :- 86.7 % and P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">CE</inf> :- 17.85%. This results in financial assistance for initiatives aiming at reducing the effect of climate change and create renewable energy sources. According to this research, perovskite solar cells should be improved in terms of their efficiency and stability in order to promote sustainable industry and to stimulate invention in clean energy solutions. This would be carried out to achieve both of these environmental objectives. Orienting perovskite solar cells in line with the world aim of creating a more sustainable future will help to reach this ambition. This alignment will define how this goal will be reached.

articleTitle: Watch Classification Using DL Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive pipeline for detecting and classifying Rado watch models in high-quality images using state-of-the-art deep learning techniques. The proposed approach sequentially integrates four main stages: YOLOv5 for initial object detection, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for precise segmentation of the detected watches, Real-ESRGAN to enhance image quality through super-resolution on the segmented watch regions, and Vision Transformer (ViT) for final model classification. This pipeline is specifically designed to address the challenges in luxury product identification, where achieving high accuracy and preserving intricate details are essential. Experimental results on a diverse dataset of watch images indicate that this approach achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 95% in detection and a classification accuracy of 93%, surpassing traditional methodologies. The results underscore the effectiveness of this integrated approach, combining cutting-edge detection, segmentation, enhancement, and classification techniques to deliver a reliable solution for applications in luxury product classification and digital marketing.

articleTitle: Fake News Detection on Social Media Platforms Using Deep Learning Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Most Smartphone users prefer their phones to read news via various social platforms on the Internet. The news site publishes news and provides the source of identity verification. Humans are ineffective in distinguishing between true and false facts and make false news a threat to the logical truth, undermining the credibility of democracy, journalism, and government agencies. With the development of new technologies, finding a strategy to reduce the spread of false news or rumors that could harm society in any way is critical. Online clients are usually vulnerable to attack, and all content they run on web-based network media is generally considered reliable. Therefore, mechanized identification of fake news is essential to maintain a significant online media and informal organization. Believing in rumors and pretending to be news is harmful to society. A lot of effort is required to stop the rumors and focus on correct, verifiable news pieces, especially in developing countries. As a result, we offer a model for detecting fake news, a computational style analysis based on natural language processing that can effectively recognize text retrieved from social media Fake News using hybrid Hybrid model-based deep learning techniques.

articleTitle: Enhanced Power Quality and Efficiency in Electric Vehicle Charging with Interleaved Boost and PSFB Converters
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents the design, modeling, and simulation of an interleaved boost converter integrated with a phase-shifted full-bridge (PSFB) DC-DC converter, optimized for electric vehicle (EV) charging applications. The system achieves a stable, ripple-free 400V DC output, regulated by a proportional resonant (PR) controller, essential for maintaining a reliable DC supply. The PSFB converter, employing zero-voltage switching (ZVS), reduces losses and enhances efficiency, making it ideal for high-power applications. Results show a consistent unity power factor across a broad input voltage range (180V-325V), and steady-state battery charging with 48.5V at 34A. This design illustrates the capability to maintain stability and power quality under varying input voltages and load conditions, advancing the effectiveness of EV charging infrastructure.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Smart Helmet System for Enhanced Road Safety and Accident Prevention
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: An Arduino-powered accident detection helmet designed to enhance motorcycle safety. The helmet incorporates an alcohol sensor (MQ3) to prevent intoxicated riders from starting their bikes. The system also features an IR sensor for anti-sleep detection, triggering a buzzer and flashing LEDs at the back of the helmet if the rider's eyes remain closed for more than five seconds. This feature aims to alert other road users and potentially prevent accidents caused by drowsiness. The helmet includes 4 LEDs at the back for increased visibility during night time riding, further contributing to rider safety. Data on helmet usage and accident fatalities suggests that many lives could be saved if all bikers wore helmets. This innovative helmet aims to address multiple safety concerns and contribute to a safer riding experience for motorcyclists. The Arduino powered Helmet is a ground breaking innovation that elevates motorcycle safety and connectivity, providing riders with a smart and proactive system to improve their riding experience and reduce hazards.

articleTitle: Efficient Algorithm Analysis Of Kidney Images On FPGA
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The field-programmable gate array (FPGA) offers an effective solution to meet the high-performance requirements of real-time digital signal processors. IP cores developed on FPGAs benefit from the programmable logic's flexibility, efficient timing, and adaptability in algorithm modification, coupled with the processing power provided by the embedded processor. Integrating image processing into this sector is an ideal addition, especially in the growing field of edge detection, which is crucial in areas like image pattern recognition, machine learning, and data processing. This paper presents a case study focused on kidney CT scan images for edge detection, utilizing the Sobel and Canny edge detection techniques on the target FPGA device, xc7z020clg484-1. An IP core was designed and generated using VIVADO software, converting image pixels into binary form for pre-processing through these edge detection algorithms. The algorithms were simulated and synthesized on the xc7z020clg484-1 FPGA, with the entire design implemented in Verilog code to create the IP, which connects to the DMA controller throughout the system. This IP core can process multiple CT scan images simultaneously, making it valuable for various biomedical applications. The primary aim of this research is to compare the Sobel and Canny edge detection algorithms to identify the best approach for developing an IP core, evaluated by metrics such as total power consumption, CPU time, execution time, LUT count, and FF usage. The resulting IP core is efficient and conserves resources, making it suitable for other embedded applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Crop Health Monitoring: A ResNet50 Approach to Automated Plant Disease Severity Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Plant diseases significantly impact agricultural productivity, making it essential to accurately assess not only the presence of disease but also its severity. This paper presents a deep learning-based framework using ResNet50 to predict plant disease severity across multiple levels (Healthy, Mild, Moderate, and Severe). The system is designed to process plant leaf images, perform augmentation to improve robustness and classify disease severity with high accuracy. The proposed method leverages labelled and pseudo- labelled datasets to enhance the model's performance through data augmentation and training on unlabelled images. The results demonstrate the model's effectiveness in distinguishing between varying levels of disease progression, providing valuable insights for early intervention and optimized crop management strategies. This platform is crucial for automating plant disease severity monitoring, and aiding decision-making processes for timely interventions in agriculture.

articleTitle: Fake Review Detection using Random Forest Classifier
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In recent years, online review plays crucial role in the modern consumer experience to provide the valuable insights into the performance and quality of the products and services. Most of the consumers take a decision about purchase of online product based on the reviews. In the view of customer all the reviews are genuine. But nowadays many of the businesses manipulated the reviews of their products by inserting the fake reviews to misleads the consumer to buy wrong product. There is a need of the effective mechanism which can identify the fake reviews and increases the trustworthiness of the online reviews. Many researchers working on the different techniques available in different domains such as Machine learning, NLP, Opinion Mining, etc. In this paper the fake reviews are identified using the random forest classifier along with different challenges identified for improvement. The amazon reviews dataset has been tested for 90000 reviews to achieves accuracy up to 79.47%.

articleTitle: Dual-Environment Dehazing Using Enhanced U-Net for Indoor and Outdoor Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an Enhanced U-Net architecture designed to achieve 99 percent dehazing efficiency for both indoor and outdoor images. The core enhancement involves replacing standard convolution layers in the encoder with dilated convolution layers, which expand the receptive field without increasing the number of parameters. This modification allows the model to capture broader contextual information, crucial for dehazing images with complex environmental variations. Additionally, we replace the conventional ReLU activation function with Leaky ReLU, which prevents neuron inactivity by allowing a small gradient for negative inputs. This choice enhances the network’s learning capability, especially in scenarios involving low-intensity regions or darker images, which are common in dehazing tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our architecture outperforms traditional U-Net models, achieving superior performance in terms of PSNR, SSIM, and visual clarity, particularly for challenging haze conditions in diverse lighting and scene settings. The architecture efficiently balances model complexity and dehazing precision, making it a robust solution for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Single Master Single Slave Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a Single Master Single Slave Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) system implemented on an FPGA. SPI is a communication protocol that enables data transfer between devices by designating master and slave roles. Despite its utility, existing peripheral communication protocols have limitations. While parallel communication requires extensive wiring and is prone to noise and crosstalk, serial communication can be slower, consume more power, and result in lower throughput. This study aims to develop an SPI module optimized for single-slave operation. Simulations conducted using AMD Vivado confirmed the module's functionality, and the design was successfully implemented on a Nexys 4 DDR FPGA board. In conclusion, the Single Master Single Slave SPI module was effectively designed and verified.

articleTitle: Design Of Robust Controller for Ball and Beam
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In this study, fuzzy logic controllers, PID, PD, and fractional-order PID are used to build a dependable control system for a ball and beam setup. Due to its extreme nonlinearity and instability, the ball and beam system presents considerable difficulties in preserving stability and accurate control in the face of uncertainties and shocks. Four control strategies—fuzzy logic controllers, fractional-order PID, proportional-derivative (PD), and proportional-integral-derivative (PID)—are created and put into practice to handle these problems. The PID controller balances fast reaction times with little overshoot by reducing steady-state error and offering comprehensive control. With an emphasis on improving stability and transient responsiveness while lowering the risk of overshoot, the PD controller streamlines the control architecture. By using fractional calculus, the fractional-order PID controller improves performance when managing nonlinearities and gives the user more control over the dynamics of the system. Linguistic variables are also used by the fuzzy logic controller to address system uncertainties and enhance flexibility. During the design stage, develops a mathematical model for the ball and beam system.

articleTitle: Optimization of Nusa Penida Electrical System: A Simulation Approach for Cost and Emission Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Nusa Penida is one of Indonesia's outer islands, territorially part of Bali Province. The electrical system in this area is separate from Bali's electrical grid and is supplied by a 20 kV interconnection from a hybrid solar-wind-diesel power station, which connects Nusa Penida, Nusa Lembongan, and Nusa Ceningan islands. The average solar radiation is 5.34 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/day with an average wind speed of 4.4 m/s. These conditions can be utilized to develop renewable energy generation in the region. This paper discusses the feasibility of the hybrid power plant established under the natural conditions and the equipment specifications used in the hybrid system in Nusa Penida, taking into account economic factors and the emissions produced. The expected outcome is to determine how the lowest LCOE can be achieved, as well as emission reduction factors, to create the most optimal electrical system structure.

articleTitle: Optimization Strategies for Interior permanent magnet Motors in Electric Vehicle Propulsion: Maximizing Average Torque, Minimizing Ripple Torque through Parameter Modification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Interior permanent magnet (IPM) motors are very efficient and have a high power density. This means that they perform better and use less energy in a variety of applications, especially in industrial and electric car systems. Because the rotor contains embedded magnets, IPM motors also feature compact designs and improved torque management, which all add to the overall dependability and efficiency of the system. It also comes with drawbacks such as cost, Because rare-earth magnets are used in the rotor of Interior Permanent Magnet (IPM) motors, manufacturing costs may be greater, which could raise the total cost of the system. To optimize its performance, we conducted a comparative analysis by adjusting parameters such as air gap, diameter, stack length, current, and number of turns in steps while keeping the base motor's geometrical parameters constant. Our goal was to identify the motor configuration that delivers the highest average torque and lowest torque ripple for each parameter variation. Additionally, we integrated the best results from each parameter modification to design a motor that meets the required average torque while minimizing torque ripple. All motors were analyzed under common specifications including a supply voltage of 60V, rated current of 15A, an average torque of 9.55 N-m, and a rated speed of 3000 RPM.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity in Medical Cyber-Physical Systems Using Blockchain and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Medical Cyber-Physical Systems (MCPS) are essential in modern healthcare, enabling real-time patient monitoring, diagnosis, and treatment. However, their integration of digital and physical elements exposes them to cyber-attacks, threatening both patient safety and data integrity. This paper shows a novel cybersecurity framework that combines blockchain technology and deep learning-based intrusion detection to protect MCPS. The proposed model uses a deep DNN-based intrusion detection system (IDS) to categorize medical data as either normal or malicious. Blockchain technology is incorporated to ensure secure, tamper-proof, and decentralized storage of patient information. To improve detection accuracy and reduce false positives, feature fusion techniques, processed through convolutional neural networks (CNNs), are applied. Ethereum-based blockchain ensures that medical data remains confidential and resistant to unauthorized alterations. The system’s effectiveness is validated using a healthcare dataset, showing a marked improvement in detection accuracy, precision, and recall over traditional methods. This integrated solution strengthens the safety and reliability of MCPS, protecting patient data while maintaining efficient data shared between medical devices and healthcare networks. Future research will focus on real-time applications and scaling the model for larger healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Challenge Response Protocol using Multivariate Polynomial Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to define the meaning of a multivariate public key using two or more multivariate encrypted parties A and B which targets to improve the existing multivariate public key encryption. Two polynomials are created by a central authority for the protocol's setup phase. The client generates a public key using a secret key, then uses his secret key to respond to a challenge the server issues and submits it to the server. The response is hashed to ensure its security. Any design, including ones with physically unclonable functions, can use this multivariate polynomial cryptography scheme since it is appropriate for post-quantum computing and quantum resistant encryption. This protocol, which protects the CCA technique of post-quantum communications, validated the promise of multivariate polynomials for information security. The work makes an effort to portray polynomial implementation and polynomial contribution as security-sensitive jobs.

articleTitle: Integrating Open-Source LLMs with Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Obstetrics and Gynecology Domain
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In this research paper, we address the integration of Large Language Models (LLM) with Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to enhance clinical decision support and address patient doubts in the Obstetrics and Gynecology (OBGYN) domain. The research mainly tries to explore on How open source LLM’s can effectively retrieve and generate the relevant responses in the OBGYN domain. The research methodology includes two components: Data Ingestion, which reads the input text data and stores it to a vector database in an embedded format and Data Retriever-Generation, which retrieves the relevant information from the vector database and use it for accurate response generation. The method includes data collection from esteemed medical databases, LLM model selection, integration with RAG and evaluation of the generated outputs. The methodology uses Bio-Mistral 7B fine-tuned LLM with PubMed Bert embeddings. The LLM responses are evaluated using the Ragas framework, context precision and context recall to measure the performance of retrieval system, faithfulness to measure hallucinations and answer relevancy to measure how relevant the answers are to the input query. The evaluated results confirm that the research has improved the accuracy as well as the contextual relevancy of the information in the OBGYN domain. This research provides a robust architecture for integration of Artificial Intelligence for supporting clinical decision making and information retrieval in specialized medical domains. This research can be extended with the upcoming advancements in the field of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science.

articleTitle: Implementation of Automatic Braking System in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This project helps to make driving safer by detecting and responding to obstructions automatically. It has ultrasonic sensors that are used in continuously monitoring the car’s distance with any objects or obstacles. The system applies the braking mechanism, when it detects an obstacle at a predetermined safe distance, either slowing down or stopping the vehicle hence avoiding accidents. Real time data handling and decision making of the intelligent braking system ensures the overall road safety. This technology is aimed at reducing road accidents, enhancing overall road safety. This system is designed to enhance vehicle safety by automatically detecting and responding to obstacles. It uses ultrasonic sensors to continuously monitor the distance between the vehicle and potential obstructions. The intelligent braking system incorporates real-time data processing and decision-making to ensure accurate and timely responses.

articleTitle: Signbridge-Audio to Sign Language Translator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The lack of communication options for Deaf and hearing people, some may say creates a significant social disadvantage in accessing the often-bare essential services. In contrast to acoustically communicated sound patterns, sign language communicates ideas freely through manual and body language. It can be used by those who have trouble speaking, by those who can hear but cannot talk, and by regular people to interact with those with hearing impairments. By automatically converting spoken words into hand gestures, this project creates a web-based interface that allows hearing-impaired individuals to communicate with normal people in real time through sign language interpretation. Two major phases of the system Speech-to-text technology interprets oral input into textual output. Next, the text is run through Natural Language Processing (NLP) algorithms leveraging the Natural language toolkit (NLTK) to be syntactically parsed in the context of sign natural rules. The last phase translates the parsed text into sign language gestures which involve hand shapes, orientation, and body movements to convey the visual meaning of a message. This system could be used to greatly reduce the communication barriers experienced by people with hearing loss and deafness using Machine Learning (ML) to continuously improve accuracy, enhance quality of life, and provide a more inclusive society between the deaf community in our daily interactions within an ever-growing world.

articleTitle: Saline Level Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The most important and primary commandment for hospitalized patients is to be carefully examined and treated, with adequate nutrition/medicine provided at the appropriate time. Aside from the different therapies they receive from doctors, saline therapy is the most fundamental treatment for dehydration, which improves their condition. However, the patient must be continuously always supervised by the nurse, which is not always practicable due to the large number of beds and other responsibilities. Unfortunately, the patient's blood begins to flow back into the saline tube due to unforeseen circumstances and carelessness. In many situations, the outcome is fatal or life-threatening. To protect their lives from essential consequences and unconditional flows, a smart saline bottle level monitoring and alert system must be designed. The proposed system offers an appropriate approach for sensing saline flow rate and monitoring it utilizing an IoT platform.

articleTitle: Advanced Feature Engineering and Model Improvement for Sarcasm Detection Using Deep Learning Architectures
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Sarcasm detection, crucial for enhancing sentiment analysis and human-computer interaction, poses challenges due to its nuanced, context-dependent nature. This study investigates advanced feature engineering and model enhancement techniques to improve sarcasm detection using deep learning. Traditional models often falter with sarcasm's complexities, so we propose a hybrid approach combining contextual embeddings, syntactic patterns, and sentiment-aware features. We test deep learning models like LSTM, GRU, and Transformer-based architectures, incorporating attention mechanisms and pre-trained models like BERT for focused analysis. Our method uses sarcasm-specific cues, with data preprocessing and augmentation. We employ Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) and PCA to optimize feature space, and evaluate on public sarcasm datasets. Results show improved accuracy and robustness, highlighting applications in social media analysis, customer feedback, and content moderation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Skin Cancer Detection Through Hybrid Convolutional and Ensemble Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: One of the most prevalent types of cancer is skin cancer and millions of people suffer from it across the globe with melanoma being the most dangerous type if not treated at an early stage. Accurate and timely diagnosis is crucial in the management of skin cancer but traditional diagnosis methods like dermoscopy, is largely dependent on the skills of qualified dermatologists which makes it subjective and susceptible to variation among observers. In this sense, deep learning and machine learning approaches have a lot of potential in automating skin cancer classification and enhancing its accuracy for better early intervention and patient outcomes. This paper presents the analysis of the performance of several models, i.e., CNN + Random Forest, DenseNet201, MobileNetV2 and ConvoMixer + CatBoost on HAM10000, ISIC and PAD-UFES-20 datasets. The experimental results indicate that DenseNet201 achieved an accuracy of 91.8%, MobileNetV2 reached 87%, and the combination of ConvoMixer and CatBoost obtained 66% However, the CNN + RF model outperformed all of the other models achieving 96% accuracy revealing the effectiveness of hybrid approaches for skin cancer classification on a reliable and scalable manner. Future work could include investigating transformer-based models, such as Vision Transformers (Suns et al.) and Swin Transformers (Liao et al.), which are able to allow better global context within the data. Also federated learning may be used to enable the use of multi institutional databases without compromising the privacy of patients. In addition, self supervised learning approaches could also help alleviate the reliance in a substantial amount of annotated datasets thereby increasing accuracy and robustness in practical and clinical situations.

articleTitle: A Federated Transfer Learning Framework with Differential Privacy for Secure Monkeypox Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Monkeypox, a viral disease characterized by skin lesions and rashes, is rapidly spreading all over the world. Early detection is essential to contain the disease. Various image classification techniques, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Transfer Learning, have been developed to accurately detect monkeypox from skin lesion images. However, using centralized patient data for model training raises privacy concerns. This paper proposes a Federated Transfer Learning (FTL) framework with Differential Privacy (DP) to address these issues. The framework uses a modified MobileNetV2 model for image classification at each client and shares only aggregated weights with the central model. Gaussian Noise, a DP technique, is applied to enhance privacy. The framework is evaluated using AUC-ROC and compared with existing models. Results show that it performs well against other classifiers while preserving patient privacy.

articleTitle: IoT Based Fire and Motion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper shows system that uses the Internet of Things (IoT) to detect fire and motion detection system which is designed to work in real time and provide emergency alerts within the given region instantly. The system combines fire detectors, small computer units and allowing all parts to communicate in real time whenever needed. The fire detection module employs smoke and temperature sensors to ensure that a fire outbreak in its initial state is detected with high precision. While passive PIR motion sensors bring about the motion detection module to interact with its users. This server helps security officials take quick actions when alerts are triggered. The tests show that the system is very accurate in detecting events like fire and movement. This means it can help prevent problems during a disaster by responding quickly.

articleTitle: 3- Pole Waveguide Band Pass filter used for Microwave P2P in 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The use of 5G applications has become increasingly significant in recent years. Since the Transmitter and Receiver antennas are located many kilometers apart, effective microwave components are required to bridge this distance. The 3-Pole Waveguide Band Pass filter design, which is utilized for microwave Point to Point, was reported in this study. The pass band frequency range in millimeter wave range is 27 GHz to 31 GHz. This filter is helpful because there isn't a regularly used active filter in the millimeter-wave frequency range. In this paper, an optimized Waveguide Band pass filter design with good Insertion loss is presented. This filter will be employed in Point to Point 5G applications. Additionally, the suggested filter exhibits improved return losses of -21.02 dB, -22.03 dB, and -23.07 dB, while the insertion loss does not surpass -0.02 dB in all three bands.

articleTitle: A CLIP-based Video Question Answering framework with Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Video analytics utilizing Video Question Answering (VideoQA) techniques to develop AI systems capable of comprehending and responding to user-specific questions from the content of the custom video datasets. The proposed system detects objects from the custom video datasets using YOLO v8, a deep learning-based object detection algorithm driven by the provided questions. The SORT algorithm helps to track detected objects throughout the entire video. Also, significant frames are extracted from the input questions utilizing a pre-trained model Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) specialized for analyzing video clips. The proposed model comprises video processing where the raw video data is analyzed and transformed for further analysis. Subsequently, questions are encoded and processed facilitating the integration of natural language understanding into the system. The proposed model integrates video comprehension with questions and enables it to correlate the content of the videos with the queries posed by the user. Finally, the model generates answers to the questions asked, accompanied by the selection of the most pertinent frame from the video based on similarity scores. The explainable LIME algorithm enhances the interpretability of the frame with the highest similarity score. This selection process ensures that the provided answers are grounded in the relevant visual context, enhancing the overall quality and relevance of the responses generated by the system. The model exhibited superior performance when applied to specialized custom video datasets.

articleTitle: Parkeezy: An IoT and Machine Learning-Based Parking System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is an expanding area of ongoing research and deployment, particularly in addressing urban mobility challenges. As the population and reliance on transportation grow, efficient parking becomes increasingly important. The abstract points out the need for an organized outdoor parking solution by highlighting the prevalent issues associated with conventional parking systems in smart towns and cities. Developing a Smart Parking Management System project, that makes use of IoT, represents a game-changing approach. The system maximizes space utilization, reduces congestion, and improves user experience by incorporating cutting-edge technologies such as OpenCV, as well as machine learning tools. Real-time data, reservation capabilities, and secure access control all contribute to a long-lasting and user-friendly solution. This paper promotes efficient parking infrastructure use, which aligns with environmental goals. It is concerned with economic efficiency, maximizing revenue for operators, and assisting businesses. Through constant user-driven enhancements, the Smart Parking Management System proposed in this paper aspires to be a scalable, adaptable, and vital aspect of modern infrastructure in cities, fostering an evolutionary shift toward sophisticated and feasible urban living.

articleTitle: A Compact Quad-band Planar Antenna for LoRa IoT Applications
