publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This work proposes a compact, Quad-band, high-efficiency Long Range (LoRa) planar antenna for IoT applications. LoRa is adopted in several settings: connected cities, smart irrigation, Mechanization, and the biosphere. These proficiencies create LoRa a good and economical option for wireless networking over far distances and in energy-efficient devices for IoT applications. The antenna has dimensions of 80mm X 50mm X 1.6mm. Mainly this antenna operates at four frequencies 0.9, 1.2, 1.8, and 4.9 GHz. The resonant frequency 0.9 GHz is applicable for LoRa Applications, and the remaining frequencies 1.2, 1.8, and 4.9 GHz are applicable for IoT applications.

articleTitle: Optimizing Torque in Synchronous Reluctance Motor: A Parameter-Based Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The SyRM motor has salient features has emphasizing simplicity, efficiency, high power factor but, this motor suffers from torque ripple, as described in this research article. The SyRM compare the average — torque and torque – ripple by modifying different parameters like Barrier length, Tooth tip angle, No. of Turns, Airgap, Slot Depth, Tooth tip depth, Currents, Tooth tip angle and Stator bore. Keeping the base motor geometrical parameters constant and again compare the average torque ripple by changing different parameters. Pick out the best motor, which has highest average torque and torque ripple in each parameter change and modelled a motor combined with these hybrid changes to obtain highest average torque and lowest torque ripple. All these machines are modelled and analyzed with a common specifications as supply voltage of 60V and rated speed of 3000RPM.

articleTitle: On Road Wireless Electric Vehicle Charging Prototype using Solar Panel
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents a wireless electric vehicle (EV) charging system, enabling continuous energy transfer while in motion. The system utilizes solar panels to generate DC voltage, converted to AC by an inverter, powering transmitting coils embedded under the road. These coils produce an alternating magnetic flux, inducing an AC electromotive force (EMF) in receiving coils attached to the vehicle. The induced EMF is rectified by rectifier and regulated using a TP4056 module and IC7805, charging the vehicle's battery. This innovative approach eliminates range anxiety, reduces battery size and weight, and enhances safety and convenience. Wireless power transfer mitigates electrocution risks and enables automatic charging initiation. The system facilitates dynamic wireless charging, ideal for EVs in motion or during brief stops, complementing static charging methods.

articleTitle: Collision Prevention System - Specializing in Animals Equipped with Distance Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The rising incidence of vehicle-animal collisions poses a serious threat to both human safety and wildlife. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to collision avoidance and animal detection using computer vision techniques, with a specific focus on generic animals. Our system employs a trained convolutional neural network (CNN) model to accurately detect animals in real-time from input video streams. The methodology integrates image processing techniques to identify animals within complex backgrounds and estimate their distance from the vehicle. A distance threshold calculation is incorporated to dynamically evaluate collision risk. Upon detecting an animal within a defined proximity, the system initiates a breaking and alert mechanism to mitigate collision risks. This automated solution not only enhances road safety but also contributes to wildlife conservation efforts. Experimental results demonstrate the system's high detection accuracy and robustness in diverse environments, affirming the potential for scalable implementation in rural and wildlife-prone areas. This study contributes to advancing collision avoidance technology through the integration of AI- driven visual processing and real-time alert systems.

articleTitle: Designing a smart drinking vessel utilizing UV sterlization for water purification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This disclosure presents a novel drinking vessel that utilizes ultraviolet (UV) light technology to sterilize water. This vessel features a hollow body specifically constructed to contain the liquid intended for sterilization, alongside a manually operable lid that allows for easy access. Central to its functionality is a sophisticated control system, which includes a sensing unit to monitor the status of the liquid and a switching and timing unit that generates activation signals for the UV lamp. The UV lamp activates to emit ultraviolet light upon receiving a signal, thereby sterilizing the liquid within the vessel over a predetermined time frame. This mechanism ensures that users can enjoy safe, purified drinking water at their convenience. The design also incorporates an ergonomic handle, enhancing portability and ease of use. Overall, this drinking vessel represents a significant advancement in personal hydration solutions, combining practicality with cutting-edge sterilization technology to promote health and safety in daily life.

articleTitle: Advanced Wearable Mine Safety System with Enhanced Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper describes the newly developed enhanced wearable protection system specifically developed to help protect the lives of coal miners by constantly assessing essential environmental/Fitness parameters. This advanced system uses multiple sensors to detect gas concentrations, temperature, humidity, dirt, heart rate, BP, and falls. It also has an emergency button for the alarm indicators as well. Sub-GHz RF technology permits long-range communication in an underground way. The effectiveness and efficiency of this system has been established through simulation, making it a dependable solution for underground protection control.

articleTitle: Design of Ground Station Antennas for Tracking of LoRa based Satellites at 433MHz Amateur Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: A Real Time ¼ Ground Plane antenna operating at 433MHz for tracking of LoRa based satellites is proposed. The Work Intends to develop different antennas for the proposed ground station. The developed antennas were designed, simulated to compare and contrast various features of antenna design. The simulated antennas were physically realized and connected to a ground station made of ESP module and LoRa module which are interconnected using Internet of Things to the internet to the online interfaces like VayuVani and TinyGS Ground Stations where satellite passes and tracking of Satellite telemetry packets are managed. It was found that the ¼ GP antenna was better in receiving packets from the LoRa based satellites. It was evident from real time tracking that the proposed ¼ Ground plane antenna could receive telemetries from slant range of around 3101.0 Km with more than 4000 Telemetry packets over a period of time.

articleTitle: Towards Low-Complexity VVENC Encoding: Challenges, Strategies, and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Versatile Video Coding (VVC) offers compression efficiency improvements of 50% and 75% compared to High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) and Advanced Video Coding (AVC), respectively. However, the VVC encoder software (VVENC), while efficient, is extremely complex and unsuitable for real-time encoding. This paper examines the overall complexity of VVENC by profiling the time consumption of its individual stages. We identify the key contributors to the encoder’s computational load. Although various efforts have been made to reduce the complexity of specific stages, such as the Transform and Quantization units, these reductions have not significantly lowered latency. As a result, real-time encoding remains out of reach. This paper highlights these challenges and explores possible strategies to reduce the overall complexity of the encoder, aiming for more efficient future implementations.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Hexagonal Patch Antenna with Star-Shaped Slot for 5G NR N257 Band and IoT Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This article proposed a hexagonal-shaped antenna with star-shaped slot in patch and Defected Ground Structure (DGS) for N257 frequency band, which operates in 26-29 GHz. The designing and analysis of the proposed antenna is carried out through Ansys HFSS. Proposed size for the antenna is 48×36×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The antenna is having a working bandwidth ranging from 26 GHz up to 29 GHz and have high Impedance matching, particularly at 28 GHz for 5G NR Applications, which is achieved by combining hexagonal shaped radiator and star-shaped slot and partial ground plane. The proposed antenna is having an impedance matching of 50 Ω. The proposed antenna is operating at a Peak Gain of approximately 8.2 dB at 28 GHz and radiation efficiency around 75%. It also supports a Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) of less than two across the entire operating bandwidth, with excellent Impedance matching. In addition, the value of active reflection coefficient for this proposed antenna is -62.9 dB. Available bandwidth of 26-29GHz i.e. N257-band, allows antenna to work across a wide range of real life applications, such as Internet of Things (IoT), 5G mm Wave technology, satellite communication and various other new technologies.

articleTitle: Economic And Emission Load Dispatch Using Modified Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The modern power system has evolved in complexity, with increasing interconnections and rising power demands. The focus has shifted towards improving performance, enhancing customer satisfaction, and delivering low-cost, reliable, and clean energy. In light of these changes, the scarcity of energy resources, environmental concerns, and rising generation costs have underscored the need for optimal economic dispatch (ED). Since power stations vary in distance from load centers and have differing fuel cost functions, the distribution of load must be optimized to minimize generation costs. This paper presents the economic dispatch problem is addressed for three and six-unit systems using MPSO, with comparisons to conventional methods for cases both with and without transmission losses. Results show that MPSO outperforms traditional optimization methods, which often converge to local optima.

articleTitle: mBERT: A Query Refinement Model for Marathi Word Sense Disambiguation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Word Sense Disambiguation involves determining the appropriate meaning of a word within a given context. Natural language processing continues to face challenges related to ambiguity. Reducing these ambiguities for applications such as machine translation, data extraction, information retrieval, query response systems. In this paper, the proposed mBERT model for word disambiguation in Marathi query refinement show good performance with accuracy of 92.5%. This accuracy shows the model's proficiency in correctly interpret the intended meanings of ambiguous words within Marathi queries. With a precision of 91.2%, the model effectively minimizes false positives, ensuring that the refined queries remain relevant and meaningful and recall score is 90.8%, shows its capability to retrieve the most relevant information from the query context. The model's balanced performance is further highlighted by a high F1 score of 91.0%, which reflects a harmonious blend of precision and recall.

articleTitle: Advanced NDRE Techniques for Precision Crop Monitoring and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Monitoring chlorophyll content is essential for assessing plant health and detecting early stress, yet traditional methods are often labor-intensive and prone to inaccuracies. An automated system utilizing the NDRE index offers a solution, employing NIR and RE spectral bands to calculate chlorophyll levels accurately across large datasets. Advanced image segmentation and machine learning techniques enhance precision, making the NDRE index a reliable indicator values below 0.5 point to potential deficiencies, while values above 0.5 signify healthier chlorophyll levels. Automation minimizes human error and accelerates evaluation, enabling early stress detection and proactive crop management. This efficient, data-driven approach supports sustainable agricultural practices and improves productivity, proving invaluable in modern crop monitoring and decision-making.

articleTitle: Contextual Sentence Embedding using Base Difference Procedure (BDP) Vectorization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Embeddings are crucial component in NLP applications since neural networks operate on numerical data rather than natural language. However, generating sentence embeddings typically requires training models on specific datasets, which is computationally expensive, time-consuming and infeasible in case of dealing with different kind of tasks (dataset) under same domain. This paper presents a approach to generate fixed-size sentence embeddings without extensive training on specific dataset.Leveraging pre-trained models trained on large datasets, our methodology produces fixed-size sentence embeddings by performing certain operations on the word vectors (obtained by pre-trained model) of any sentence to be embedded into a fixed size vector. Our approach significantly reduces computational cost, time for vectorization and independent of any specific dataset, making it an efficient alternative for obtaining sentence representations for different NLP tasks which comes under same domain.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Antennas for Underwater Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper explores the electromagnetic wave communication capabilities of antennas operating at the 900 MHz ISM band in different media: air, freshwater, and seawater. The paper focuses on the performance of two antenna designs: the Rounded Edge Bow-Tie Antenna (RBTA) with middle-sliced modifications and the Bicone Antenna. Simulations performed using Ansys HFSS examine key parameters such as return loss, gain, and radiation patterns to provide insights into their behavior across diverse environments. The results show that the RBTA enhances short-range underwater communication, with significant performance variations influenced by the medium’s dielectric properties. The 900 MHz frequency selection improves signal penetration and stability but also presents challenges, particularly in seawater, where high conductivity increases signal attenuation. This work advances understanding of antenna design for effective underwater communication.

articleTitle: Fall Detection System for Elderly People using Piezoresistive Textile Pressure Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Fall detection systems are critical for ensuring the safety and well-being of the elderly and others with mobility challenges. This paper presents the design and development of a fall detection system employing a textile pressure sensor constructed using piezoresistive Velostat material, sandwiched between two layers of conductive fabric. The developed pressure sensor is embedded into wearable socks, offering a flexible and unobtrusive solution for continuous monitoring. The piezoresistive nature of the sensor allows it to detect pressure changes when a fall occurs, capturing real-time data. The system processes this data to distinguish between normal activities and fall events based on predefined thresholds. The fall detection system also features wireless communication for real-time alerts, ensuring immediate assistance can be provided when a fall is detected. This approach provides an efficient and non-intrusive method for enhancing safety, with potential applications in home care and healthcare monitoring for at-risk individuals.

articleTitle: A Fuel Cell Powered Soft Switched based Buck Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In recent decades, fuel cells (FCs) have attracted significant interest in the automotive industry owing to their ease of use, silent operation, outstanding performance, and modular design. Traditional converter switching induces power losses during the switching process, hence diminishing system efficiency. This research examines solid oxide fuel cell-powered buck-boost converters using zero voltage switching (ZVS), requiring few auxiliary components, namely one capacitor and one diode. This paper presents an innovative method for the design of the ZVSABuck-Boost converter, which operates as a resonant buck-boost regulator. The@buck-boostcconverter has been modeled, and the necessary output simulation results and waveforms are shown. MATLAB Simulink was used to develop and simulate an 850 W prototype model.

articleTitle: Automatic Pesticide Spraying Drone
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Drones are emerging technologies in agriculture, replacing manual pesticide spraying due to harmful side effects on personnel. It is designed to reduce time and labor costs for farmers. This paper aims to develop a software system that finds and classifies plant diseases using image processing techniques for effective disease detection in agricultural applications. Using the software simulation, this drone assists the farmer in choosing the land's coordinates for accurate use of pesticides on land. Additionally, it facilitates the drone's automated takeoff and landing.

articleTitle: Retinal Disease Detection for Low Resource Devices Through Pruned and Quantized CNNs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Retinal disease diagnosis is one of the crucial step for preventing vision loss, especially in conditions such as Diabetic Retinopathy(DR), Glaucoma, and Age-related Macular Degeneration(AMD). In this paper, we propose an efficient approach for retinal disease classification using lightweight convolutional neural networks (CNNs) deployed on a low-resource device, the Raspberry Pi 4. To address the limitations of resource-constrained hardware, we employ model optimization techniques, including pruning and quantization, to reduce computational requirements while maintaining classification accuracy. The proposed system is evaluated on the Messidor datasets. Our optimized MobileNet and EfficientNetLite models decreased the accuracy scores by 1.5% to 2%, while reducing inference time by over 50% and memory usage by 45%. These results show the feasibility of deploying real-time retinal disease models on edge devices for telemedicine and mobile health in resource-limited settings.

articleTitle: Efficient Framework for Pet Adoption and Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The fragmented landscape of pet adoption in India presents significant challenges, including the lack of essential features such as breed filters and effective communication channels, complicating the process for both prospective pet owners and sellers. Moreover, the absence of a centralized database and educational resources for new pet owners exacerbates inefficiencies and contributes to pet abandonment. Aims to address these issues by creating a centralized, user-friendly platform. The current system's deficiencies necessitate a novel approach to streamline the pet adoption process. Our methodology involves the development of a robust platform featuring advanced search filters (breed, gender, age, and price) and comparison tools to aid in informed decision-making. A significant innovation of our platform is the emphasis on communication, providing direct messaging and inquiry options to foster transparent and trustworthy interactions between adopters and sellers. Additionally, the platform offers extensive educational resources and guidance for new pet owners, promoting responsible pet care and thereby reducing instances of pet abandonment.

articleTitle: Property Price and Rent Prediction System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) has revolutionized various sectors including speech recognition, product recommendations, and healthcare. This research focuses on applying ML techniques to address challenges in real estate market prediction. The unpredictable nature of property prices creates significant difficulties for buyers in making informed decisions. This research proposes a multi-algorithm housing price prediction model, integrating SVM, Random Forest, and GBM approaches, with Random Forest demonstrating superior predictive performance. The model considers various factors influencing property prices, enabling buyers to make data-driven decisions without excessive reliance on intermediaries. This paper presents the methodology, implementation, and comparative results of these algorithms in the context of real estate price prediction.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Fractional Wireless Power Transfer Systems via Scattering Parameters
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Analyzing fractional-order wireless power transfer (WPT) systems through scattering parameters reveals several advantages over their classical counterparts. Compared to the fixed value in classical systems, the most notable improvement is the variable nature of the critical coupling coefficient in fractional systems. This contrasts with the classical system, which shows optimal performance only under near-perfect coupling conditions and within a narrow frequency band around the resonant frequency. The efficiency analysis reveals that the fractional system maintains a higher transfer efficiency at lower coupling coefficients by leveraging higher frequency operations, a capability not present in classical WPT systems. The ability to optimise performance through frequency adjustment rather than physical coupling modifications represents a significant advancement in wireless power transfer technology.

articleTitle: A Trapezoidal-Structured Switched-Capacitor Balancing Circuit for Li-ion Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The existing switched capacitor (SC)-type equalizers are less reliable and inefficient because of their bulkiness and high cost. Therefore, to suppress the drawbacks of existing switched capacitor equalizers (SCEs), a Trapezoidal-Structured SCE (TSSCE) is proposed with optimal cost, compact size, good efficiency, and better equalizing speed. The constructional feature of the proposed equalizer allows it to provide multiple optimal balancing paths with a minimal number of capacitors. An asymptotic relationship of the effective resistance model is presented, which gives an in-depth idea about the behavior of capacitors and switches in slow and fast switching limit regions. A simulation model is made, with four cells connected in series. Simulation analysis ensures the performance of the proposed converter. TSSCE achieves a better equalization speed and efficiency with only n capacitors for n number of cells, making the topology cost-effective and faster than the existing equalizers.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a 3-Ø Grid-Interfaced 100 kW Solar Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)

authors.preferredName: S K B Pradeep Kumar CH

abstract: The present work decides the quantity and quality of power consumed by utility grid from the 100 kW of solar photovoltaic system connected to the 3-phase grid. An Internal Model Current Control Method (IMCCM) is used to control the Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) of a grid-tied solar system. The proposed control method aims to capture the maximum power from the PV array and addresses issues related to power quality. It also works to reduce harmonics and improve power factor in changing conditions. The filter parameters of voltage source inverter are used for the designing of the proposed IMCM. The maximum power from a solar PV system is tracked using a simple Perturb and Observe (P&O) Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) method combined with a DC-DC converter. The proposed model is simulated using MATLAB/Simulink platform. It is identified that the control method works well in both steady state and change in irradiance.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a High-Efficient Nanowire FET for Emerging Logic Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The continuous demand for miniaturized, high-performance logic devices that requires the development of new transistor technologies brings NWFETs into consideration as a very promising alternative to conventional MOSFETs. Although MOSFETs are highly efficient, their scalability and efficiency are greatly hindered by short-channel effects, leakage currents, and excessive power dissipation at smaller nodes. This paper attempts to design and simulate an optimized NWFET for logic applications to overcome these issues. The work uses TCAD simulation tools to evaluate some of the critical performance metrics which include threshold voltage, Ion/Ioff current ratio and subthreshold slope. Preliminary results show that NWFETs have better electrostatic control while consuming less power and being more scalable; thus, they overcome the limitations of MOSFETs in subsequent technology nodes. Results are implemented through detailed comparative analysis work with existing MOSFET structures.

articleTitle: Compact and Secure Image Encryption for IoT Systems Employing ECC and AES Hybrid Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This study focuses on development of a secure and efficient image cryptosystem optimized for IoT devices. The proposed technique addresses the and resource constraints of IoT devices, it introduces a hybrid encryption approach where an amalgam of algorithms such as Arnold’s Cat Map, ECC, Diffie-Hellman (ECDH), AES is used for optimized encryption for the image data. This combination ensures compact, secure, and resource-efficient encryption suitable for IoT systems. The system is evaluated through various performance metrics demonstrating its effectiveness in lightweight cryptography applications while ensuring high levels of security against common cryptanalytic attacks.

articleTitle: Leveraging Blockchain for Cloud Log Security and Compliance in AWS
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: As the demand for cloud computing is increasing across the globe, more and more companies are shifting their data and IT infrastructure to the cloud. Log data integrity, security, and compliance are important in such an environment for anomaly detection, audit trails, and regulatory adherence. However, traditional log management systems suffer from tampering, data breaches, and centralized control. Recent research has, therefore, looked into blockchain technology as a means of boosting cloud security. This paper presents a blockchain-based approach to securing and authenticating AWS cloud logs. Utilizing the blockchain’s immutable and decentralized nature, the proposed system hashes AWS CloudWatch logs with a Python-based system and records the hash on the Ethereum blockchain via a smart contract. This process prevents undetected log alteration or deletion. The smart contract manages log hash storage and verification, with the Infura node facilitating Ethereum blockchain interactions and MetaMask handling private keys and test ETH. Original and modified log hashes are compared to assure the system’s efficiency, besides computing transaction costs and processing times. The findings suggest blockchain’s potential as a solid framework for log data security and compliance, offering a decentralized, tamper-proof log storage solution that enhances cloud infrastructure security and compliance for organizations.

articleTitle: Fog Node Selection and Task Scheduling in Fog Computing Environment: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Fog Computing is an emerging field of cloud computing, resides between cloud and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. IoT consists of sensors, cameras, actuators, and other smart devices. IoT devices generate latency-sensitive tasks in real-time environment and forward them at fog layer. Fog layer analyses the incoming tasks, schedule them, and allocate resources for their processing. In delayed-sensitive applications, task scheduling and their allocation are much complex as they require quick responses, and real-time decisions. Additionally, frequent node failures are common due to diverse characteristics of fog computing. It becomes more crucial and essential to identify reliable fog nodes at fog layer for further computations. This study presents a systematic review of existing fog node selection methods with consideration of different selection parameters. Furthermore, the study reviews existing scheduling and allocation methods under heuristic, meta-heuristic, optimization, and machine learning approaches. The study reviews existing techniques with consideration of delay, energy usage, costs, network usage, and reliability. As per the comparative analysis, the study identified reliability as most significant issues in the existing approaches. Finally, the study provides future research suggestions to improve the reliability in fog environment for improving QoS.

articleTitle: In-Memory Computation using Asymmetrical Schmitt Trigger SRAM cell
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In-memory computation (IMC) addresses data processing directly within the memory itself. This approach eliminates much of the data transfer overhead, offering the potential for faster, more energy-efficient computation. This work looks into an Asymmetrical Schmitt Trigger based SRAM cell design for In-memory computation (IMC). The circuit is implemented using 45 nm technology, functions with an input frequency of 200 MHz, and uses a 0.8 V DC operating voltage. Performance metrics for the re-implemented asymmetrical Schmitt trigger SRAM cell recorded at 200 MHz include an output delay of 3.75 ns, an average power consumption of 3.12 µW and an energy per bit consumption of 3.58 fJ which shows 15.36% improvement in the energy per bit consumption at a cost of 52.44% decrease in SNM. The paper proposes an IMC based circuit for the implementation of all logic gates using Asymmetrical Schmitt Trigger SRAM cell.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Strategies for Optimizing MLM Performance: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This review examines the pivotal role of data analytics in optimizing Multi-Level Marketing (MLM) operations amid evolving market challenges. It highlights key strategies such as predictive analytics for customer acquisition, customer segmentation for personalized marketing, and sales funnel optimization to enhance conversion rates. Additionally, the paper discusses churn prediction and retention strategies to foster long-term customer loyalty, along with performance tracking for distributors to boost productivity. While data-driven approaches offer significant benefits, challenges such as data integration, the need for data literacy, and ethical considerations regarding privacy must be addressed. Ultimately, leveraging data analytics is essential for MLM companies seeking sustainable growth and competitive advantage.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Different Antenna Shapes (Hexagonal, Pentagonal, Circular, Octagonal Triangular) for Sub-6 GHz Band in 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The growing demand for high-speed and reliable communication in the sub-6 GHz frequency band of 5G networks has driven extensive research into optimizing antenna designs. This paper explores the performance of antennas with unconventional geometries, such as hexagonal, pentagonal, circular, octagonal and triangular shapes, tailored for the sub-6 GHz band. These shapes are evaluated based on parameters such as gain, bandwidth, radiation efficiency, and impedance matching. Through simulation and experimental results drawn from existing studies, this research presents a comparative analysis to determine the suitability of each shape for 5G communication applications.

articleTitle: A Random Key Generation & Transport Mechanism for Wireless Data Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The emergence of 4G, 5G and IoT based communication has brought a revolutionary turnaround in wireless data networks. Data communication can’t be imagined without wireless channels. Wireless communication channels are very prone to information security attacks. The wireless devices are having some constraints like battery issues, limited computational power etc. Keeping this in mind, a random key generation and transportation method for wireless data networks is presented in this paper. We show that generated keys are totally random and then transmitted via secure and robust steganographic method to the receiver. The proposed method is easy to implement and very optimized in terms of computational overheads.

articleTitle: Adaptive Scheduling Using the MQTT Protocol in the IoT Based on Environmental Sensing and Network Load
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Adaptive protocols that react to shifting network and ambient conditions have been developed in response to the Internet of Things' (IoT) increasing need for effective communication. The MQTT protocol is used in this study's adaptive scheduling strategy to maximize IoT communication by modifying transmission intervals in response to network congestion and environmental variables like pressure, temperature, and humidity. Using a mathematical model Adaptive scheduling enhances throughput, lowers latency, and improves energy economy in contrast to fixed scheduling which has trouble adapting. According to experimental data, adaptive scheduling performs better than fixed techniques, offering notable energy savings, decreased latency, and increased throughput. This opens the door for more effective and sustainable IoT communication.

articleTitle: Evaluation of tweets for disaster management
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Natural disasters can strain traditional communication channels, making social media platforms like twitter essential for real-time crisis updates. This research uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) to classify disaster-related tweets efficiently, offering critical insights for emergency responders, aid organizations, and policymakers. The proposed system applies advanced NLP techniques, such as text preprocessing, TF-IDF and Word Embedding for feature extraction, and Random Forest algorithms for classification. Optimized for accuracy, this model supports faster, more informed decision-making, improving disaster response. With ongoing advancements in NLP and machine learning, we anticipate further enhancements that will strengthen such systems, aiding in disaster impact reduction.

articleTitle: The Future of Traffic Management: Embracing AI for Sustainable Urban Mobility
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The management of traffic in urban environments has become increasingly complex due to rapid urbanization and the growing number of vehicles on the road. This literature review synthesizes research on various traffic management systems and technologies, focusing on solutions such as real-time image processing, IoT-based systems, wireless sensor networks, and deep learning models. The review highlights key advancements, including intelligent traffic controllers utilizing real-time video analytics, IoT for congestion control, and AI-enabled traffic monitoring systems.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Technology Based UPQC To Enhance The Power Quality Problems In Grid Integrated To Solar Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The country's need for power is growing with a rise in population. Sources of renewable energy, such as the sun and wind can be employed alongside conventional sources to satisfy peak load demands. Photo-Voltaic (PV) energy generation has lower installation and production costs than wind energy generation. However, due to the extensive use of nonlinear electronics, grid-connected PV systems have increased power quality problems. The proposed system will overcome above problem and it will give the better performance results also reduce the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) other than the traditional techniques. To create the most electricity possible from photovoltaic solar energy plants, the Deep Learning algorithm technique is suggested. The proposed system presents a novel technique for enhancing grid-integrated PV system based power quality. When compared to a traditional UPQC-based PI controller, the creation of an advanced DNN (Deep Neural Network) controller-based UPQC (Unified Power Quality Conditioner) enhances power quality and lowers THD value for the grid integration of PV system. The suggested approach is used to analyze the performance of power quality concerns in the MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Deep Insights of Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI) Degradation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: As the global semiconductor industry moving towards successive generations, the density of Integrated Circuit increased, therefore reliability issues became critically high, among them Negative Bias Temperature Instability is prominent one. NBTI degraded the PMOS transistor’s behavior when subjected to inverted gate voltage. The impact of NBTI can be referred to as threshold-voltage adjustment of PMOS, degradation in drain-source current, and reduction in speeds of device. An increase in temperature with negative gate stress is the primary introduction that degrades the Gate Oxide, which in turn causes all these adverse effects. Hence, stress analysis is required for any device before designing circuitry so that when circuits are drawn, high performance of the circuits is ensured. Out of many reliability problems affecting PMOS transistors at the nanoscale level, NBTI occupies center stage. This paper discusses stress-variation-dependent impact of NBTI for 22nm bulk CMOS inverter circuit over the period of 10 years.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of MAC Unit with Various Parallel Adders
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) Unit is a crucial component in all DSP Applications, due to its ability to perform high-speed arithmetic operations. This research aims to design and implement an 8-bit MAC Unit capable of performing multiplication and accumulation operations. The MAC Unit employs the same multiplier but integrates different adders such as Kogge-Stone, Ladner-Fischer, Carry Look-Ahead adder, and Ripple Carry Adder. The structures were formed using Verilog Hardware Description Language (HDL) and implemented on Xilinx ISE, with simulation carried out using ModelSim.

articleTitle: Anti-Spoofing: A Bio Finger Print Recognition Method using Pattern Matching Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Biometric authentication plays a key role in smart environments, with finger print recognition being one of the most common methods. Fingerprint readers scan and store fingerprint data, comparing it during login attempts to verify identity. While effective, these systems are vulnerable to spoofing using materials like wax, clay, or gelatine. Criminals sometimes exploit this technology to access personal information. Two main algorithms, minutiae matching and pattern matching, are used for recognition. Minutiae matching compares unique points on fingerprints, while pattern matching analyzes surface thickness, curvature, and ridge patterns. However, injuries to the fingercan make identification challenging. Advances now integrate sensors to detect pulse and sweat glands, enhancing security. Fingerprint recognition is widely employed in legal systems for identity management, but the technology relies heavily on intact surface patterns for accurate matching.

articleTitle: SCADA Based Centralized Power Management System for Grid-Connected Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: It is difficult to meet the rising electricity demand with the existing fossil fuel-based power plants. Increasing the capacity of fossil fuel-based power plants beyond a certain limit is not feasible. Microgrids are offering a way to address the issue of supply and demand mismatch with the help of renewable energy-based distributed energy resources (DER) and energy storage systems (ESS). This paper proposed a Centralized Power Management System (CPMS) for efficient operation and control of a grid-connected microgrid. An IEEE 13 bus system is modified to serve as the Microgrid test system by adding DERs and ESS at strategic locations. SCADA-based CPMS is chosen to send the control commands to various Microgrid components. To make the system cost-effective and reliable, the CPMS appropriately allocates power from DERs and ESS to the loads. Numerous case studies are carried out using Simulink/MATLAB, based on various system dynamics to ensure the validity of the CPMS.

articleTitle: UV Exposure Real-Time Monitor for Skin Protection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Excessive exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation significantly increases the risk of skin damage, sunburn, and skin cancer. Despite public awareness, many individuals lack real-time personalized monitoring solutions for their UV exposure. This paper presents a wearable UV exposure monitoring device designed to provide continuous real-time feedback using the GUVA-S12SD UV sensor and ESP WROOM 32 microcontroller. The system tracks UV-A and UV-B radiation levels, processes the data, and transmits it to a mobile application via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). The device aims to empower users to take timely preventive measures, raising awareness and reducing the health risks associated with prolonged UV exposure. This project supports preventive healthcare initiatives, promoting user engagement in skin health management through sustainable and energy-efficient technology.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Medical Image Denoising with Efficient NetB3 and Pix2Pi
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Medical imaging is crucial in modern healthcare, providing key insights into anatomy and aiding in illness diagnosis, tracking, and treatment planning. Images from technologies like MRIs, CT scans, X-rays, and ultrasounds allow easy visualization of structures, detection of anomalies, and monitoring of medical conditions. The traditional image denoising techniques have less interpretability because they don't rely on data training. In this work, a hybrid approach to image denoising is presented that makes use elements of EfficientNetB3 and Pix2Pix models. The EfficientNetB3's efficient scaling and feature extraction capabilities, combined with the Pix2Pix's image-to-image translation capabilities, enable the model to effectively remove noise while preserving essential image features. The proposed structure provides a viable way to raise both the accuracy and reliability of medical image assessments.

articleTitle: Fog Vision for Roads and Rails
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Reduced visibility due to fog creates hazardous conditions in sectors like transportation, aviation, and outdoor navigation. This research introduces a dual-purpose monitoring system that combines fog detection with real-time object recognition, designed using a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ paired with an OV5647 5MP IR cut camera sensor and QuickDetect, a real-time object detection module utilizing Python and the Ultralytics YOLO v8 model [1] [2]. Our system processes video frames to assess fog presence through contrast and blurriness indicators via OpenCV while simultaneously detecting objects with YOLO v8, enabling a comprehensive environmental assessment. The unified design of fog detection and object recognition on a single, affordable platform allows the system to evaluate visibility and detect relevant obstacles, enhancing situational awareness. Preliminary testing has indicated promising results, with efficient detection of fog and accurate identification of objects. This project contributes a practical and accessible solution for safety improvements in low-visibility environments, with potential applications in smart transportation, environmental monitoring, and autonomous navigation.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of A Soft-Switched Buck-Boost Converter for Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The Buck-Boost converter, that plays a significant role in scaling up or down the DC voltage at the output with no need of any intermediary ac stage, is the most notable dc-dc converter. Conventional converter switching causes power losses during switching, which lowers system efficiency. In this study, buck boost converters are powered by zero voltage switching (ZVS)-based soft switching with less auxiliary component i.e., using one capacitor and diode. The ZVS Buck-Boost converter, which functions as a resonant buck-boost regulator, was designed using a new methodology in this study and is used as battery charging system. The buckboost converter has been modelled, and the required output simulation results and waveforms are shown. MATLAB Simulink was used to create and simulate an 850 W prototype model.

articleTitle: Voice Authentication at Scale: A Room Level Approach for Smart Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In light of the rapid expansion of voice- activated smart devices, achieving reliable and secure voice authentication across multiple rooms presents complex challenges. Traditional voice authentication methods fall short in differentiating speakers based on their specific locations, raising security risks in shared spaces. This study introduces a room-level voice authentication model that leverages both spatial audio features and machine learning techniques to distinguish users based on their physical environment. By analyzing room-specific acoustic signatures and integrating them with biometric voice characteristics, the proposed approach strengthens access control, offering a scalable solution that addresses the unique demands of multi- room setups. Performance evaluations indicate high accuracy in correctly identifying both speaker and room, confirming the method’s potential for secure, location-based voice authentication in smart homes and office spaces.

articleTitle: Using LLMs for Querying and Understanding Long Legislative Texts
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: With over 2,000 bills being passed in the California State Legislature each year, it can be very confusing for the average citizen to understand what is being approved. This process can be made much easier with recent advancements to large language models (LLMs). Specifically, using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). This research paper will study two different approaches to using LLMs to answer questions about bills passed in our state legislature. The first approach will employ standard RAG protocol to scan and retrieve any information relevant to the user’s prompt and summarize it in an easy-to-read manner. Our second approach expands the context window of the model to consider a wider range of legislature when scanning for keywords entered by the user. By analyzing the performance of each LLM, we can find the best model that guarantees contextually rich answers to any questions surrounding the state legislature.

articleTitle: Text Summarization in local language
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This research focuses on abstractive text summarization techniques for regional languages, specifically Hindi. It employs a Transformer-based model to generate rephrased summaries from datasets of local language news articles. Preprocessing includes tokenization and embedding creation with FastText. Summarization quality is evaluated using ROUGE scores, precision, recall, F1-Score, and human assessment. The study addresses challenges related to Hindi syntax and semantics, aiming to improve regional language processing by providing concise, coherent news summaries and enhancing information access.

articleTitle: Biogas Resource Estimation for Different Temperature Zones in India using a Thermal model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Biogas-based energy generation is gaining attention due to its on-demand availability, renewable nature, and environmental benefits. India holds significant potential for dairy farm-based biogas systems, where energy output depends on daily biogas volume, influenced by the chemical properties of waste and the substrate temperature within the digester. The substrate temperature is driven by solar irradiance and ambient temperature. This paper introduces a methodology to estimate cow dung-based biogas resources using a thermal model and Typical Meteorological Year (TMY) data. A thermal model calculates the hourly slurry temperature for floating drum digesters using TMY data from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory. Seven different zones are identified based on solar irradiance and temperature. Monthly biogas yield factors, based on data from International Renewable Energy Agency, IRENA, give the daily electrical energy production capacity for these zones in India.

articleTitle: Real Time Traffic Light Timing Optimisation Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: A major problem especially in urban areas is traffic congestion which causes increased travel times, pollution, and compromises safety. This paper presents the design of the Smart Traffic light timing Management System, optimized in real-time traffic light timings using reinforcement learning techniques. This system scans data from different sources, including vehicle count in a network and waiting time of the vehicle at a traffic stop, which are utilized to continuously to alter traffic signals based on current situations. Utilizing reinforcement learning algorithms, the system continuously learns and adapts to changing traffic scenarios, striving for minimal congestion. The simulations run in SUMO (Simulation of Urban Mobility) indicate a noticeable reduction in wait times and improved flow across roads. The results form the basis for the inclusion of advanced data analytics in traffic management: it represents an effective method of mitigating urban congestion problems. The study concludes that by leveraging real-time data and machine learning, the traditional traffic systems can be transformed into an intelligent responsive network, capable of enhancing the efficiency and safety of urban transportation.

articleTitle: Review on 6G Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The demand for multimedia data services is rising rapidly, and while 5G has been implemented globally, it won’t sustain the projected mobile traffic growth. To address 5G’s limitations, Sixth Generation (6G) communication has been proposed. Operating in the mm wave and terahertz regions, 6G will offer faster data rates, exceeding 100 GB/s, and a wide frequency range from 300 GHz to 3 THz. This study explores 6G's promising capabilities, including high-quality imaging, precise localization, and advanced sensing. 6G technology will heavily integrate machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI), especially within smart cities, where they will be pivotal in improving citizens' quality of life. By combining diverse components for monitoring, analysis, planning, and execution, 6G-enabled applications will support advanced services that enhance urban living experiences, address environmental challenges, and provide more efficient solutions across industries.

articleTitle: Key Gas Analysis – Comparison of Methodology to promote Mixed Oil Insulation for Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In the power industry, the two most common types of market equipment are distribution transformers (DT) and power transformers (PT). The dielectric fluid is essential to PT and DT's dependable operation. In this study, several dielectric fluids that are measured according to combustible gases called key gases (KG) that dissolve in oil are compared. The primary faults that are recognized under various fault circumstances are where the KG is created. For clarification, the ratio of KG to the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) fault classification has been stated. The ongoing research confirms how crucial it is to combine various insulating fluids to lower the KG and lengthen the life of PTs and DTs. Lastly, a brief overview of the potential for further study on mixed insulating oil. This initiative aims to prolong transformer life, lower pollutant levels, and support environmental sustainability in a mutually beneficial manner.

articleTitle: Enhancing Renewable Energy Integration: An Analysis of Bidirectional Converters And Multilevel Inverter Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The need to mitigate resource depletion and the adverse environmental consequences associated with fossil fuels is driving the world's growing reliance on renewable energy sources like wind and solar. However, because energy supply is inherently unpredictable, integrating renewables presents problems for system stability and power quality. In order to control energy flow, maintain grid stability, and enable the integration of renewable energy sources at a lower cost, power electronic converters—particularly switched-mode power converters—are essential in tackling these issues. This paper offers a thorough analysis of several converter topologies, such as multilevel inverters, which maximize AC power supply with the least amount of harmonic distortion, and bidirectional DC-DC converters, which control bidirectional power flow for energy storage. It focusses on different multilevel inverter types, such as neutral-point-clamped, flying capacitor, and cascaded H-bridge designs, and converter classes, such as non-isolated and isolated bidirectional DC-DC converters. A Single stage power conversion system named Dual leg DC-AC converter is also explored. Furthermore, innovative semiconductor technologies like GaN and SiC as well as control strategies are examined to improve reliability, efficiency, and power density. By supporting the design of high-performance power converters, this study hopes to contribute to the development of robust and sustainable energy systems in the future.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Smart Irrigation Control System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The development of a smart irrigation system is critical in addressing water conservation and enhancing agri-cultural practices. The design and implementation of a control system aimed at regulating water delivery to plants based on critical factors such as soil moisture, weather conditions and specific plant requirements is presented in this paper. The system assimilates various control methodologies, including PID control, root locus analysis, frequency response analysis, state space representation, and digital control techniques. For modeling, simulation and testing of the system, ensuring a comprehensive evaluation of its performance, Simulink is used. The proposed smart irrigation system demonstrates substantial improvements in water use efficiency and plant health by dynamically adjusting irrigation schedules in response to real-time environmental data. To further promote this technology in sustainable agriculture, future enhancements and real-world applications are discussed.

articleTitle: IoT Driven Transformer Condition Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Transformers are essential parts of electrical distribution networks, therefore power systems rely heavily on their condition. This study introduces an Internet of Things (IoT)-based transformer condition assessment system that assesses transformer health using real-time data collection and sophisticated analytics. A number of variables, including temperature, current, oil level, and electrical loads, are used by the system. A cloud platform displays this data for analysis and tracking. This makes it easier to predict maintenance and prompt interventions prior to the development of critical failures, as well as to spot patterns and anomalies. An intuitive dashboard improves transformer management decision-making by giving operators relevant insights and alarms. By putting this IoT framework into practice, power distribution systems operate more efficiently overall, optimize maintenance schedules, and save operating expenses.

articleTitle: Stress Detection Using SVM and Virtual Assistant
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This paper presents a chatbot model designed to detect stress in users through simple yes-or-no questions. Utilizing a Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm, the model achieves high accuracy in identifying stress levels and provides users with actionable advice or medical recommendations. The chatbot’s user-friendly interface is built using Anaconda Navigator and Python, ensuring ease of use for non-technical users. The model achieves a 100% accuracy rate on the given dataset, making it a promising tool for stress detection and early intervention.

articleTitle: Wireless EV On Road Charging System (WEVOS)
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In the present decade, there has been an increase in the adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs). This surge in demand for EVs is driven by the global push to combat climate change and reduce the dependency on fossil fuels. Traditional wired charging systems limit the mobility of EV owners, requiring frequent stops at charging stations and extensive infrastructure. This paper aims to address these challenges by developing a wireless EV charging system. WEVOS utilizes electromagnetic induction to transfer energy between the coppercoils embedded beneath the ground and the vehicles. The proposed system aims to efficiently charge EVs regardless of whether the vehicle is in motion (dynamic) or stationary (static). This presents a potential reduction in the economic and logistical burdens associated with installing and maintaining extensive charging infrastructure, encourages EV adoption, reduces range anxiety, thus offering an effective alternative to conventional charging methods.

articleTitle: SmartLib: Automated Library Management with RFID and Mobile Alerts
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The Manual Library Management System used at present is quite complex process which might take lot of time as it includes maintaining the records of personal, membership and fine details where there can be chances of making error and missing the important details. To avoid such issues and make the procedure much efficient The Automated Library Management System is introduced, which basically consists of a microcontroller (Arduino Nano ATmega328p), RFID along with a LCD display. BLYNK software is used in this process to emerge. Automated Library Management System is made simple and more flexible for managing the library, the updates, status of the member and other details would apprise through the software which would reduce the time and cost is feasible which could be profit for the user, hence manual efforts are reduced.

articleTitle: Analysis of Voltage and Load profiles of a rural distribution Feeder in Madhya Pradesh
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: In rural India, power supply reliability and quality in distribution feeders often suffer. A major challenge is low voltage issues, worsened by increased demand from agricultural loads, especially irrigation pump sets. These heavy loads, typically during peak agricultural periods, strain local distribution infrastructure, causing voltage drops, inefficiencies, and reduced productivity. This paper examines the impact of agricultural loads on the Kuwa feeder in Thikri tehsil, Barwani district, Madhya Pradesh, focusing on voltage sags, fluctuations, and instability. Detailed voltage and load analysis highlights the causes of low voltage problems and their impact on power delivery reliability. Based on the analysis, voltage conditions have been evaluated, revealing normal operating conditions eliminating undesirable conditions of overvoltage, voltage fluctuations and reverse power flow to the grid. The study focuses on the importance of regular voltage monitoring and analysis to ensure consistent power quality and to design sustainable solutions.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Improved Fast Charging Technique for Modern Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The design and development of an electric car charging station in this study are suitable for a wide range of electric vehicles. When designing and integrating charging stations into real-time projects, the availability and accessibility of charging infrastructure are key considerations. Whereas developing charging systems, charging standards, procedures, charging levels, charging time reduction technique and control strategy. Most of the tasks carried out by the grid with this e-storage technology include charging and controlling the batteries in electric cars. The rules and modelling used in this research design are described in order to demonstrate how the charging system behaves. The findings demonstrate the capability of the suggested paradigm and the potential of the to demonstrate how the charging system behaves. The findings demonstrate the viability of the suggested paradigm and the potential of the charging systems.

articleTitle: Integrated Electromagnetic, Thermal, and Vibration Analysis for High-Performance Synchronous Reluctance Motor Design in Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The SyRM motor is known for delivering high power density at a low cost, thanks to its reluctance principle. Unlike synchronous motors that require starting methods and are not self-starting, the SyRM motor doesn’t need any starting mechanisms. Additionally, it can maintain a constant speed under various conditions, overcoming changes in loads such as underloads or overloads through synchronizing torque. The absence of torque ripples is a notable advantage. However, one drawback is its inability to vary speed, limiting its application in scenarios where speed control is necessary. Another limitation is the higher copper losses due to the presence of three-phase windings, compared to DC motors. To address these issues, Finite Element Analysis was conducted on the SyRM motor, encompassing electromagnetic, thermal, and vibration analyses. The parameters examined included torque, flux linkage, speed under load, E-NVH modal, time harmonics (1D with harmonic order vs amplitude characteristics), harmonic order and angle characteristics, space harmonics (with respect to space order vs angle characteristics), and space order vs amplitude characteristics. Additionally, a polar plot was employed in this analysis. In the thermal analysis, a schematic overview revealed insights into the motor’s thermal behavior. The motor specifications used for modeling were a voltage of 60V, current of 15Amp, speed of 3000rpm, and power of 3KWatts.

articleTitle: Dynamic Equilibrium in Robotics:Techniques and Applications for Self Balancing Robots
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Self-balancing robots have become a key focus in robotics and control system studies since they are capable of standing on two wheels as an upright system. In the implementation of these systems, PID control, Linear Quadratic Regulation, fuzzy logic as well as reinforcement learning in machine learning is applied to control the balance and motion of the robots in the robots in different environmental conditions. This article reviews literature on self-balanced robots over the last half century moving beyond mechanical and electrical designs to control strategies including how double loop control incorporated PID control and how this has now shifted to machine learning. It also describes sensor fusion techniques where a Kalman filter or complementary role filters is employed sensor’s accelerometer data and gyroscope data towards the assistance of estimating how tilted the robot is to the ground in degrees. Practical examples are also analyzed from personal devices such as the Segue, to education and robotics research. The paper also investigates the current challenges in the field including sensor drift , battery life, and especially the need for real time adjustment to varying environmental conditions such as bumpy terrain or perturbations. A number of ways are suggested such as using better sensors, control strategies and low power actuators which all improve balance robot systems. The study finishes with the discussion of the optimal developments, particularly focusing on the use of overcome strategies of controls using artificial intelligence for bringing about more flexibility and independency to self-balancing robots.

articleTitle: Filtering Methods, Assessment Criteria, and Prospects for Image Denoising
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Image denoising is a crucial step in image acquisition and processing that helps improve the image quality by removing the unwanted noise. In this paper Gaussian and median filters are used as denoiser and performance is evaluated using some of the key metrics like Mean Squared Error (MSE), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Feature Similarity Index Measure (FSIM), Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Correlation Coefficient. A denoiser with low MSE, high PSNR, values of 1 for SSIM, FSIM, and Correlation Coefficient. Reported results are better in comparison to existing for better image quality.

articleTitle: Wrist Fracture Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)

authors.preferredName: Kothapalli S. V. V. R. Srinivas

abstract: Effective treatment of wrist bone fractures depends on early and precise identification. The finding shows that disparities in accessing timely emergency services translate into adverse patient outcomes, especially in regions with fewer healthcare facilities and extended distances, mostly rural areas. Distal radial fractures or wrist fractures are among the commonly encountered musculoskeletal injuries and the treatment and subsequent management depend on timely and precise identification of the fracture pattern. This paper discusses a wrist fracture detection scheme using a deep learning approach for diagnosing wrist bone fractures from X-ray images which can close the health disparities due to the lack of adequate early diagnosis. and his team developed the system using DenseNet-201, MobileNetV2, ResNet-50, EfficientNetV2, U-net and Inception V3 architecture because each was selected for a certain use effect patient outcome. Wrist fractures, among the most common musculoskeletal injuries, require early and accurate diagnosis to optimize treatment and rehabilitation. This project presents a deep learning-based system to detect wrist fractures in X-ray images, designed to bridge healthcare inequalities by facilitating early and automated diagnosis. The system integrates DenseNet-201, MobileNetV2, ResNet-50, EfficientNetV2, U-Net, and Inception V3 models, each chosen for specific roles. DenseNet-201, MobileNetV2, and ResNet-50 are classification networks for fracture detection while U-Net is segmentation network to segment fractured areas. Furthermore, the results using EfficientNetV2 and Inception V3 improve diagnostic capability and image comprehensiveness.This work compares the pros and cons of each model in terms of accuracy, computational time, and loss and presents recommendations for the most appropriate models for clinical applications in practice.

articleTitle: Conceptual Mechatronic Design of Robotic System for Lower Limb Rehabilitation in Post-Stroke Patients using the VDI 2206 and VDI 2225 Standard
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: This study aims to design a robotic system for continuous passive motion therapy to support lower limb rehabilitation in post-stroke patients. The design process adheres to VDI 2206 and VDI 2225 standards. Key stages include defining requirements based on anthropometric and biomechanical data, function structuring, and using a morphological matrix to explore solutions. Weighted matrices evaluated ergonomics, control precision, and safety, leading to an optimal design for knee and ankle rehabilitation. The system provides controlled, passive movement, supports up to 80 kg, and allows adjustable speed and load resistance, ensuring smooth actuation and biomechanical alignment for effective motor recovery. A Von Mises analysis of the rail-structure connector, using 304 stainless steel under a 784 N vertical load (simulating patient weight), revealed a maximum stress of 29.58 MPa and deformation of 1.12×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>, remaining within the material's elastic limit.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Automated Smart Parking Fee Management System using RFID Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Parking systems are essential for urban infrastructure, ensuring efficient vehicle management and optimal use of space. As urban areas become more congested, there is an increasing need for organised and automated parking solutions. Traditional parking systems are primarily manual, resulting in inefficiencies, long wait times and security issues. The paper presents an IoT-based smart car parking fee collection system that automates the parking and fee collection process. The proposed system employs Arduino Uno and ESP32 microcontrollers with RFID technology to regulate parking entry and exit, ensuring secure and authorised access. It is integrated with ThingSpeak to enable real-time data collection and visualisation, providing administrators with valuable insights into parking usage and fee collection. Parking fees are calculated based on the duration of stay and sent to users via email, promoting an environmentally friendly and paperless solution. The system includes an automated barrier control using servo motors, smart lighting control with LDR sensors and email notifications through the ESP32 module. This system enhances the user experience by reducing wait times and providing a seamless parking process while offering administrators the tools needed for effective parking management. This comprehensive solution effectively addresses the challenges of conventional parking systems and meets the growing demands of modern urban environments.

articleTitle: Creating an Adaptive Robot for Personalized Health Monitoring and Assistances
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: Medical robots are a groundbreaking advancement in healthcare, utilizing robotics and automation to improve precision, efficiency, and accessibility in medical procedures. They are utilized in various applications, including minimally invasive surgeries, rehabilitation, diagnostics, and patient care. Surgical robots, such as the da Vinci Surgical System, are notable examples because they allow physicians to do intricate procedures with greater dexterity and a lower chance of human error. Rehabilitation robots support patient mobility recovery by customizing therapy to meet individual needs and progress. Diagnostic robots utilize imaging technologies to assist in early disease detection and accurate diagnostics, often incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) for image analysis and pattern recognition. The emergence of autonomous and semi-autonomous robots in medical environments promises to alleviate the workload of healthcare professionals, streamline processes, and enhance response times in critical care scenarios. However, the integration of robotics into healthcare also poses challenges, such as ethical dilemmas, regulatory obstacles, and concerns regarding data privacy and patient safety. The future of medical robotics will rely on overcoming these issues while promoting innovation.

articleTitle: Demand Response Strategies in Microgrids with Electric Vehicle Loads
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
abstract: The integration of electric vehicles (EVs) into microgrids has introduced new challenges and opportunities in energy management. As the number of EVs increases, their charging demand can significantly impact the stability and efficiency of microgrids. This paper investigates various demand response (DR) strategies tailored to manage EV loads within microgrids effectively. The study explores both centralized and decentralized DR mechanisms, assessing their impact on load balancing, peak demand reduction, and energy cost minimization. The performance of these strategies is evaluated through simulations in diverse operating scenarios, considering factors such as renewable energy variability, grid constraints, and user preferences. The results highlight the potential of advanced DR techniques, such as price-based and incentive-based schemes, to optimize energy distribution and enhance the resilience of microgrids. The paper also discusses the role of real-time communication and control technologies in facilitating effective EV integration. By addressing the dynamic nature of EV loads, this research provides insights into designing efficient, reliable, and sustainable microgrids capable of accommodating growing electrification demands.

articleTitle: Auto-Assess: Automated Evaluation Platform for Enhanced SQL learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
